text:
Promenade des Anglais (French pronunciation: [pʁɔmnad dez‿ɑ̃ɡlɛ], [- dez‿ɑ̃ɡle]; lit. "Walkway of the English"; Niçard: Passejada deis Anglés, Standard Occitan: Passejada dels Anglés) is a promenade along the Mediterranean coast of Nice, France. It extends from Nice Côte d'Azur Airport on the west to the Quai des États-Unis [fr] ("United States Quay") on the east, for a distance of approximately 7 kilometres (4.3 mi).[1] It forms part of Route nationale 98, which runs between Toulon and Menton.

History
Starting in the second half of the 18th century, the English aristocracy took to spending the winter in Nice, enjoying the panorama along the coast. In 1820, when a particularly harsh winter further north brought an influx of beggars to Nice, some of the English proposed that the beggars could work on the construction of a walkway (chemin de promenade) along the sea. It was funded by the Reverend LEWIS Way and members of Holy Trinity, the Anglican church in Nice.[2][3]

The city of Nice, intrigued by the prospect of a pleasant promenade, greatly increased the scope of the work. The Promenade was first called the Camin deis Anglés (the English Way) by the Niçois in their native dialect. After the annexation of Nice by France in 1860 it was rechristened La Promenade des Anglais.

The Promenade was the site of the team time trial in the 2013 Tour de France, held on 2 July 2013. It was also featured as a start and finish location of the first two stages of the 2020 Tour de France.[4] Due to the Paris Olympics, the 2024 Tour de France concluded on the Promenade, instead of its usual location of the Champs-Élysées.[5]

Stages 8 and 9 of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes concluded on the Promenade.[6]

Modern day
For local inhabitants, Promenade des Anglais has simply become the Promenade or, for short, La Prom. It is popular with bicyclists, baby strollers, and families, especially on Sundays. It has also become a favorite place for skateboarders and in-line skaters.

2016 Bastille Day attack
Main article: 2016 Nice truck attack
On 14 July 2016, a truck was deliberately driven at revellers celebrating Bastille Day on the Promenade. The driver, 31-year-old Mohamed Lahouaiej-Bouhlel,[7] also shot at others before crossing the road in the vehicle to continue the assault. The vehicle was surrounded by police near the Palais de la Méditerranée, and the terrorist was shot dead. Eighty-six people were killed, and 458 were wounded.[8]

Primary Germanic and Norman Origin
Frankish Roots: It stems from the Old Frankish Hlūtwīg (or Chlodowech), composed of hlūt ("loud" or "fame") and wīg ("battle" or "war").
Latin and French Evolution: The name was Latinized as Ludovicus, evolved into Old French as Clovis or Louis, and was brought to Britain by the Normans after 1066 as Lowis or Lewis.

Revelation 17:8 That is as many as have not learned the providence of God, according to the faith of the Saints, shall marvel at these grievous and often changes when they shall consider, the selfsame beast, which is the Roman Empire, to have been, not to be, and to be and still molested with perpetual mutation, and yet in the same to stand and continue. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. Promenade des Anglais (French pronunciation: [pʁɔmnad dez‿ɑ̃ɡlɛ], [- dez‿ɑ̃ɡle]; lit. "Walkway of the English"; Niçard: Passejada deis Anglés, Standard Occitan: Passejada dels Anglés) is a promenade along the Mediterranean coast of Nice, France. It extends from Nice Côte d'Azur Airport on the west to the Quai des États-Unis [fr] ("United States Quay") on the east, for a distance of approximately 7 kilometres (4.3 mi).[1] It forms part of Route nationale 98, which runs between Toulon and Menton.

History
Starting in the second half of the 18th century, the English aristocracy took to spending the winter in Nice, enjoying the panorama along the coast. In 1820, when a particularly harsh winter further north brought an influx of beggars to Nice, some of the English proposed that the beggars could work on the construction of a walkway (chemin de promenade) along the sea. It was funded by the Reverend LEWIS Way and members of Holy Trinity, the Anglican church in Nice.[2][3]

The city of Nice, intrigued by the prospect of a pleasant promenade, greatly increased the scope of the work. The Promenade was first called the Camin deis Anglés (the English Way) by the Niçois in their native dialect. After the annexation of Nice by France in 1860 it was rechristened La Promenade des Anglais.

The Promenade was the site of the team time trial in the 2013 Tour de France, held on 2 July 2013. It was also featured as a start and finish location of the first two stages of the 2020 Tour de France.[4] Due to the Paris Olympics, the 2024 Tour de France concluded on the Promenade, instead of its usual location of the Champs-Élysées.[5]

Stages 8 and 9 of the 2026 Tour de France Femmes concluded on the Promenade.[6]

Modern day
For local inhabitants, Promenade des Anglais has simply become the Promenade or, for short, La Prom. It is popular with bicyclists, baby strollers, and families, especially on Sundays. It has also become a favorite place for skateboarders and in-line skaters.

2016 Bastille Day attack
Main article: 2016 Nice truck attack
On 14 July 2016, a truck was deliberately driven at revellers celebrating Bastille Day on the Promenade. The driver, 31-year-old Mohamed Lahouaiej-Bouhlel,[7] also shot at others before crossing the road in the vehicle to continue the assault. The vehicle was surrounded by police near the Palais de la Méditerranée, and the terrorist was shot dead. Eighty-six people were killed, and 458 were wounded.[8]

Revelation 17:1 The state of the Church militant being declared, now followeth the state of the Church overcoming and getting victory, as I showed before in the beginning of chapter 10. The state is set forth in 4 chapters. As in the place beforegoing I noted, that in that history the order of time was not always exactly observed, so the same is to be understood in this history, that it is distinguished according to the persons of which it treateth, and that in the several stories of the persons is severly observed in the time thereof. For first is delivered the story of Babylon destroyed, in this and the next chap. (for this Babylon out of all doubt shall perish before the 2 beasts and the Dragon). Secondly is delivered the destruction of both the two beasts, chap. 19. And lastly of the Dragon, chap. 20, in the story of the spiritual Babylon are distinctly set forth the state thereof in this chap. and the overthrow done from God, chap. 18. In this verse and that which followeth is a transition or passage unto the first argument, consisting of a particular calling of the Prophet (as often heretofore) and a general proposition.
Revelation 17:1 That is the damnable harlot, by a figure of speech called hypallage. For S. John as yet had not seen her. Although another interpretation may be borne, yet I like this better.
Revelation 17:1 The sentence that is pronounced against this harlot.
Revelation 17:3 Henceforth is propounded the type of Babylon, and the state thereof in 4 verses. After a declaration of the type, in the rest of this chap., in the type are described two things, the beast (of whom chap. 13), in verse 3, and the woman that sitteth upon the beast, verses 4, 5, 6. The beast in process of time hath gotten somewhat more than was expressed in the former vision. First in that it is not read before that he was appareled in scarlet, a robe imperial and of triumph. Secondly, in that this is full of names of blasphemy: the other carried the name of blasphemy only in his head. So God did teach that this beast is much increased in impiety and injustice and doth in this last age, triumph in both these more insolently and proudly than ever before.
Revelation 17:3 A scarlet color, that is, with a red and purple garment: and surely it was not without cause that the Romish clergy were so much delighted with this color.
Revelation 17:4 That harlot, the spiritual Babylon, which is Rome. She is described by her attire, profession and deeds.
Revelation 17:4 In attire most glorious, triumphant, most rich, and most gorgeous.
Revelation 17:4 In profession, the nourisher of all, in this verse, and teaching her mysteries unto all, verse 5, setting forth all things most magnificently: but indeed most pernicious besotting miserable men with her cup, and bringing upon them a deadly giddiness.
Revelation 17:5 Deceiving with the title of religion, and public inscription of mystery: which the beast in times past did not bear.
Revelation 17:5 An exposition: in which S. John declareth what manner of woman this is.
Revelation 17:6 In manner of deeds: She is red with blood, and sheddeth it most licentiously, and therefore is colored with the blood of the Saints, as on the contrary part. Christ is set forth imbrued with the blood of his enemies; Isa. 3:1.
Revelation 17:6 A passage unto the second part of this chapter, by occasion given of S. John, as the words of the Angel do show, in the next verse.
Revelation 17:7 The second part or place, as I said, verse 1. The narration of the vision, promised in this verse, and delivered in the verse following. Now there is delivered first a narration of the beast and his story, unto verse 14. After, of the harlot, unto the end of the chap.
Revelation 17:8 The story of the beast hath a triple description of him. The first is a distinction of this beast from all that ever hath been at any time: which distinction is contained in this verse: The second is a delineation or painting out of the beast by things present, by which he might even at that time be known of the godly, and this delineation is according to his heads, verses 2, 10, 11. The third is an historical foretelling of things to come, and to be done by him: and these are ascribed unto his horns, verses 12, 13, 14. This beast is that Empire of Rome, of which I spake, chap. 13:11, according to the mutations and changes whereof which then had already happened, the holy Ghost hath distinguished and set out the same. The Apostle distinguisheth this beast from all others in these words. The beast which thou sawest, was and is not. For so I expound the words of the Apostle for evidence’s sake as I will further declare in the notes following.
Revelation 17:8 The meaning is, that beast which thou sawest before (Rev. 13:1) and which yet thou hast now seen, was, (I say was) even from Julius Caesar in respect of beginning, rising up, station, glory, dominion, manner and stock, from the house of Julius: and yet is not now the same, if thou look unto the house and stock for the dominion of this family was translated unto another, after the death of Nero from the other unto a third, from a third unto a fourth, and so forth was varied and altered by innumerable changes. Finally, the Empire is one, as it were one beast: but exceedingly varied by kindreds, families, and persons. It was therefore (saith S. John) in the kindred or house of Julius: and now it is not in that kindred, but translated unto another.
Revelation 17:8 As if he should say, Also the same that is, shall shortly not be: but shall ascend out of the depth, or out of the sea (as was said, Rev. 13:1) that is, shall be a new stock from amongst the nations without difference, and shall in the same state go unto destruction or ruin, and perish: and so shall successively new Princes or Emperors come and go, arise and fall, the body of the beast remaining still, but tossed with so many and often alterations, as no man can but marvel that this beast was able to stand and hold out, in so many mutations. Verily no Empire that ever was tossed with so many changes, and as it were with so many tempests of the sea, ever continued so long.
Revelation 17:8 That is as many as have not learned the providence of God, according to the faith of the Saints, shall marvel at these grievous and often changes when they shall consider, the selfsame beast, which is the Roman Empire, to have been, not to be, and to be and still molested with perpetual mutation, and yet in the same to stand and continue. This in mine opinion is the most simple exposition of this place, and confirmed by the event of the things themselves. Although by the last change also, by which the Empire, that before was civil became Ecclesiastical, is not obscurely signified by these words: of which two, the first exercised cruelty upon the bodies of the saints: the other also upon their souls: the first by human order and policy, the other under the color of the law of God, and of Religion, raged and imbrued itself with the blood of the godly.
Revelation 17:9 An exhortation preparing unto audience, by the same argument, with that of Christ: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear. Wherefore, for mine own part, I had rather read in this place, Let there be here a mind, etc. So the Angel passeth fully unto the second place of this description.
Revelation 17:9 Very children know what that seven hilled city is, which is so much spoken of, and whereof Virgil thus reporteth, And compasseth seven towers in one wall: that city it is, which when John wrote these things had rule over the kings of the earth: It was and is not, and yet it remaineth this day, but it is declining to destruction.
Revelation 17:9 This is the painting out of the beast by things present (as I said before) whereby S. John endeavored to describe the same, that he might both be known of the godly in that age, and be further observed and marked of posterity afterwards. This delineation hath one type, that is, his heads, but a double description or application of the type: one permanent from the nature of itself, the other changeable, by the working of men. The description permanent, is by the seven hills, in this verse, the other that fleeteth, is from the seven kings, verses 10, 11. And here it is worthy to be observed, that one type hath sometimes two or more applications, as seemeth good unto the holy Ghost to express either one thing by divers types, or divers things by one type. So I noted before, of the seven spirits, Rev. 1:4. Now this woman that sitteth upon seven hills, is the city of Rome, called in times past of the Greeks, … i. of seven tops or crests, and of Varro, septiceps, i. of her seven heads (as here) of seven heads, and of others, septicollis, i. standing upon seven hills.

THE US$60.68 MILLION PRESIDENTIAL JET: WHERE IS THE PRINCIPLE?

Yesterday, 16th November 2026, the Minister for Government Communications, Hon. Felix Kwakye Ofosu, announced that the Ghana Air Force has taken delivery of a brand-new Falcon 6X presidential jet, acquired under a contract worth a staggering US$60.68 million.

This development raises serious questions about the consistency, credibility and principles of the government.

During the debate on the 2026 Budget, the Minority raised concerns about the government’s plans to acquire presidential aircraft. The Majority disputed our characterisation of the proposed expenditure and sought to justify the acquisition.

Indeed, it was suggested at the time that the procurement and delivery process would take several years, giving the strong indication that the aircraft would not be delivered during President Mahama’s tenure.

Yet, yesterday, barely a year later, the aircraft has been delivered. How does the government explain this remarkable turn of events?

Let us not forget that, when the NDC was in opposition, leading members of the party opposed proposals to acquire a new presidential jet, claiming that the
economic circumstances confronting the country does not justify such expenditure and that there is the need to prioritise the welfare of ordinary Ghanaians.

What has changed?

At a time when many Ghanaians continue to struggle with the cost of living, youth unemployment remains alarmingly high, and the government’s much-touted 24-hour economy has yet to deliver its promised transformation, the administration has found the resources to acquire a luxurious presidential aircraft.

The question is not simply whether Ghana requires a safe and reliable presidential aircraft. It is whether those who condemned such expenditure when they were in opposition can now defend it without adequately explaining what has changed.

What was unacceptable in opposition cannot suddenly become acceptable in government merely because the occupants of power have changed.

The apparent double standards and political inconsistency are difficult to ignore.

Ghanaians deserve a full explanation of the cost, financing arrangements, procurement process and justification for prioritising this expenditure at this time.

Accordingly, the Minority Caucus on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee will demand full disclosure and accountability from the government on this acquisition. We shall pursue the matter in Parliament and insist on answers regarding the total cost to the taxpayer, the financing arrangements, the procurement and approval processes, and the justification for the acquisition. We shall also demand the full documentation relating to the transaction.

The government must be prepared to account to the representatives of the people for every dollar committed to this purchase. Public expenditure of this magnitude demands transparency, accountability and rigorous parliamentary scrutiny.

Politics and public life must be anchored in at least a modicum of principle!

🚨 INTERESTING STORY: $AAPL IS NOW LOOKING TO LOCK IN DRAM SUPPLY FROM SAMSUNG FOR THE NEXT 4–5 YEARS.

this is bullish for $MU and $SKHY investors.

so back in August, Apple reportedly approached China's $CXMT looking for cheaper memory. CXMT wasn't willing to offer the discount Apple wanted.

then Washington pushed Apple to stay away from Chinese memory suppliers.

now Apple is reportedly finalizing a long term agreement with Samsung, starting in H1 2027, with minimum purchase volumes but pricing still tied to market conditions.

Apple is one of the biggest buyers of memory in the world. For years, it used that purchasing power to negotiate lower prices and avoid long term commitments.

today even Apple is willing to commit years ahead just to secure supply.

the interesting part is that Samsung isn't being asked to lock in cheap prices for those four or five years. Pricing would still move with the market.

it's a pretty significant change in bargaining power.

i feel for $MU, this is another encouraging sign that memory manufacturers have more leverage than they did in previous cycles. AI data centers are absorbing production capacity, and now consumer electronics companies are competing to secure what's left.

when a company as powerful as $AAPL starts prioritizing supply security over getting the lowest possible price, it tells you something about how tight the memory market has become.

🇺🇸🇮🇷🇮🇱🇹🇷⚓🌍 AJ's Morning Briefing, Tuesday, Nov 17: 🇮🇷 Iran's third Bahrain strike, a reported ☢️ dirty bomb plan, and 🇺🇸 Trump in 🇵🇭 Manila

🇮🇷 Iran's IRGC fired drones at a 🇺🇸 📡 radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in 🇧🇭 Bahrain on Tuesday, its third such attack since Friday, and 🇧🇭 Bahrain says it intercepted them. Overnight, a tanker was disabled off 🇴🇲 Oman's coast with its crew unaccounted for, as the IRGC claimed two more vessels hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz. 🇮🇷 FM Abbas Araghchi met 🇴🇲 FM Badr Al Busaidi in Muscat.

CNN reported Monday, citing seven 🇺🇸 officials, that 🇺🇸 intelligence indicates 🇮🇷 Iran is developing options for a dirty bomb or chemical attack on senior Trump administration officials in Washington. Officials say it is planning, not an imminent attack, and the White House says there are no credible threats to the 🇺🇸 homeland. 🇺🇸 👨‍💼 President Donald Trump landed in 🇵🇭 Manila and met the Quad leaders.

📍 The President:

🗓️ - Tuesday, Nov 17 (Philippine time): 🇺🇸 👨‍💼 Trump arrived in 🇵🇭 Manila, then greeted the Quad leaders at 6:20 PM and held a Quad meeting at 6:30 PM with 🇮🇳 India, 🇯🇵 Japan and 🇦🇺 Australia. It's the group's first leaders' meeting in two years and Trump's first. Trump called 🇮🇳 👨‍💼 Narendra Modi "a tough man" in front of reporters. Later: a 🇺🇸-🇹🇭 Thai trade deal signing at 7:25 PM, an ASEAN-US special summit and reception at 7:45 PM, and a US-ASEAN dinner at 8:25 PM. Protests against the 🇺🇸 war on 🇮🇷 Iran are under way in Manila, per Rappler.

🗓️ - Wednesday, Nov 18: Welcome ceremony with 🇵🇭 👨‍💼 President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Malacañang Palace at 11:05 AM, a bilateral at 11:30 AM and a lunch at 12:30 PM (Philippine time). Then on to 🇨🇳 Shenzhen.

🗓️ - Thursday, Nov 19: The Shenzhen trilateral with 🇨🇳 👨‍💼 Xi Jinping and 🇷🇺 👨‍💼 Vladimir Putin, where the White House says ☢️ nuclear disarmament and 🇮🇷 Iran are on the agenda.

⚠️ Not confirmed: Trump has said he "may" meet 🇰🇵 👨‍💼 Kim Jong Un in 🇨🇳 China, though a senior White House official said last week there were "no plans at all."

📍 Secretary of State:

🇺🇸 👨‍💼 Marco Rubio is traveling with Trump to the 🇵🇭 Philippines and 🇨🇳 China, Nov 16-19, and is joining the Quad meeting. State's public schedule lists no other events for him, and there is no Department press briefing today. Under Secretary 🇺🇸 👩‍💼 Allison Hooker is in the 🇵🇭 Philippines and 🇨🇳 China, Nov 14-20.

Deputy Secretary 🇺🇸 👨‍💼 Christopher Landau is traveling to Tajikistan, 🇹🇷 Türkiye and Turkmenistan, Nov 16-24. His Türkiye stop is in Istanbul, where he is to meet senior Turkish officials and business leaders on bilateral cooperation, commerce, energy and supply-chain security. Exact dates for the Istanbul leg weren't published.

Sunday, Rubio condemned 🇮🇷 Iran's attacks on 🇧🇭 Bahrain in a call with 🇧🇭 FM Abdullatif Al Zayani and reaffirmed the 🇺🇸 commitment to the security of Bahrain and all Gulf partners, the State Department said.

📍 Intelligence Community:

🆔 Leadership: Jay Clayton is the current Director of National Intelligence, having taken over in August per a search summary, and John Ratcliffe remains 🇺🇸 CIA director. I found no new public statements or published agendas from the DNI, CIA, NSA or DIA chiefs overnight.

🇺🇸 News involving the IC: The CNN report on 🇮🇷 Iranian dirty bomb or chemical attack options in Washington rests on 🇺🇸 intelligence. Seven 🇺🇸 officials told CNN that analysts are still debating whether Tehran can or will carry it out. 🇮🇷 Iran's UN mission "categorically rejects" the report as "false and fabricated." The White House's Lauren Bis said the US is "monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland."

📍 The FBI:

🇺🇸 The FBI, a Department of Justice law enforcement agency, confirmed "law enforcement activity in Peoria County," Illinois, Monday in the BioUrja ethanol plant case. CNN reported a suspect was arrested Monday morning and that the investigation into others continues. A bomb threat was received Friday, and an explosive device was found and neutralized Friday night, which led to an 18-hour evacuation. The FBI has not confirmed the arrest and says any charges will appear in federal court records. No motive has been announced.

🇺🇸 👨‍💼 FBI Director Kash Patel: no new agenda or statement since yesterday. His most recent public remarks I found, on Nov 11, concern three 🇮🇷 Iranian-backed operatives indicted for roles in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across the 🇺🇸 and Europe, including a foiled plot against a military base housing American troops.

📍 Terrorism and threats to the US:

🇺🇸 Beyond the 🇮🇷 dirty bomb report, no new confirmed terror attack in the United States overnight. The Des Moines arrest of a 17-year-old for a threat against Roosevelt High School, charged with threats of terrorism, is a local case with no reported foreign link.

📍 Central Command and the force posture:

⚓ 🇺🇸 USS Theodore Roosevelt entered the 5th Fleet area Sunday and is operating in the Central Command area on a scheduled deployment, per USNI News, making three 🇺🇸 carrier strike groups in the 🌍 Middle East. It is expected to relieve USS George Washington, and it's unclear how long Washington stays.

🇺🇸 Central Command denied the IRGC's Friday claim of a hit on a Bahrain radar, saying two one-way drones were shot down. I found no formal Central Command statement on today's attack. No new statements from the Central Command, NAVCENT, AFCENT, ARCENT, MARCENT or SOCCENT commanders turned up.

📍 Iran and Hormuz:

🇮🇷 - Iran side:

The IRGC said its drones hit a 🇺🇸 📡 radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base in 🇧🇭 Bahrain on Tuesday, citing "repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones." Bahrain issued a shelter alert, and explosions were heard over Manama. Bahrain says it intercepted the attack, and no impacts were reported. AP calls it the third strike on US targets in Bahrain since a roughly two-month lull.

The IRGC Navy claims a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of 🛢️ crude and a liquefied gas carrier struck mines, and 🇮🇷 Iran's regular navy claims another tanker is disabled east of the strait. None of it is verified. The US military says the southern shipping lanes are mine-free.

Daily UK defence and security brief from Think Defence, Tuesday 17 November 2026, covering the previous 24 hours.

NEWS

Crimea Bridge Shut After Reported Ukrainian Strike as Russia Hits Kyiv Crossings

The Crimea (Kerch) bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia has been closed after reports that a Ukrainian strike inflicted major damage, with images shared by a former Zelensky adviser appearing to show a section collapsed into the water; the BBC has not independently verified them. Overnight, Russian ballistic missile strikes closed Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro and damaged heating, water and some above-ground metro services.

BBC News
https://t.co/NKaUjOC9GF

Americans Urged to Keep a Low Profile in UK Amid Festive Terror Threat

US citizens in the UK have been warned to keep a low profile and remain vigilant to potential terror attacks during the festive period.

Sky News
https://t.co/zf6YvWTmDs

Water Companies Told to Act Over Fears Drought Will Extend Into Next Year

Water firms have been told to do more amid fears that the current drought will continue into next year, a national resilience concern heading into winter.

Sky News
https://t.co/Y1t8AiVf4D

UK Among Nations Funding NATO StarLift Launch Plan

Ten allies including the UK, along with South Korea, have committed to finance StarLift through the NATO Support and Procurement Agency, a launch brokerage that will help military users secure slots on commercial rockets across a network of allied spaceports. Announced at NATO Edge 26 in Izmir, it aims to make military access to space more resilient, responsive and cost-effective.

UK Defence Journal
https://t.co/UzwsNGLwAV

Russia Churning Out Jet Strike Munitions, Says Helsing UK Chief

Ned Baker, UK managing director of Helsing, told the Atlantic Future Forum that intelligence suggests Russia produces about 4,000 jet-powered long-range strike munitions a month and allies cannot afford to fire million-pound interceptors at that mass. Helsing is building a drone submarine factory in Plymouth and its SG-1 gliders are to be trialled under Atlantic Bastion.

UK Defence Journal
https://t.co/nFQ2wg8AJp

Defence Industry Must Deliver Product, Not PowerPoint, Says Former First Sea Lord

Admiral Sir Philip Jones, former First Sea Lord and now working with BAE Systems, said defence firms must deliver product rather than just PowerPoint and focus on what they can field within three years, urging governments to give industry more certainty and industry to take more risk and work more closely with smaller firms.

UK Defence Journal
https://t.co/dLxTacyOYc

CONTRACT UPDATES

DE&S Awards Rohde & Schwarz UK LSDA Communications Support Contract

Defence Equipment and Support has awarded Rohde & Schwarz UK a contract worth about £5.9 million (excluding VAT) for in-service support of Landing Ship Dock Auxiliary communications and V/UHF emergency radio from 1 June 2027, including a technical helpdesk, spares, repair and post-design activity.

https://t.co/WZVgI1KYt8

MoD Awards Atos Project McBride OCD2 Intelligence Systems Contract

The MoD has awarded Atos IT Services UK a contract worth about £3.59 million (excluding VAT) for Project McBride OCD2, developing a firm-base intelligence analysis and fusion system feeding deployed OpCIS, including a connection to the US Army Intelligence Data Platform.

Find a Tender
https://t.co/WYTsFJv7k5

DIO Plans PFI Exit Asset Condition Surveys Procurement

The Defence Infrastructure Organisation intends to use the RM6343 Estate Management Services 2 framework to procure technical and professional support for Private Finance Initiative exit activities across its estate in England, estimated at £5.17 million (excluding VAT).

Find a Tender
https://t.co/rx5pCYopyS

MoD Planning Notice for UK E-7 Wedgetail Stowage Containers

The MoD has published a planning notice for three shipsets of stowage containers, ladders and fittings for the UK E-7 Wedgetail AEW Mk1, including certification and support.

Find a Tender
https://t.co/VIq9sivOru

MoD Tenders Security Screening Equipment for HMP Dhekelia

The MoD has issued a tender for an integrated security screening capability at HMP Dhekelia in the Sovereign Base Areas of Cyprus, including an X-ray cabinet, walk-through metal detector and explosives and narcotics trace detector, valued at about €176,564.

Find a Tender
https://t.co/FawWr0g5UY

King Opens New National Cyber Force HQ in Lancashire

The King has officially opened Ribble House, the National Cyber Force's new headquarters in Samlesbury, Lancashire. The NCF, bringing together GCHQ, the MoD, SIS and Dstl, conducts cyber operations against state threats, terrorists and criminals, and the site is intended to support jobs and skills in the North West Cyber Corridor, with a Digital and Cyber Bursary now supporting 500 local students.

https://t.co/MRsfW3en53, Ministry of Defence
https://t.co/S3idRu480M

DEFENCE IN PARLIAMENT

Written Answer: MoD Will Not Disclose Number of Starshield Terminals

Answering James MacCleary, Luke Pollard said the MoD holds access to a considerable number of Starshield terminals but will not give the number for national security reasons. Starshield is used alongside other capabilities as part of a resilient satellite communications strategy that avoids over-reliance on any single provider, and is selected requirement by requirement.

UK Parliament written questions

Written Answer: Devonport 10 Dock and SWIF Programme Delayed Beyond 2027

Luke Pollard said MoD and NISTA assurance had highlighted issues with the original 2027 delivery date for the Submarine Waterfront Infrastructure Future programme. 10 Dock at HMNB Devonport has moved into construction with work on dockside buttresses, but challenges remain; the MoD is working with NISTA and the contractor to recover the programme and is reviewing opportunities to accelerate following the Nuclear Regulatory Review.

UK Parliament written questions

UK Parliament written questions

Luke Pollard said the department's naval procurement expenditure in Scotland in financial year 2025-26 amounted to £349,774,449.82 in payments, excluding VAT.

UK Parliament written questions

Louise Sandher-Jones said the MoD is assessing alternative options for training currently provided at MOD Bicester to ensure continuity of operational output; cost and feasibility estimates have been prepared but will not be disclosed for commercial reasons, and relocation costs will be met by the Home Office.

eagle8
Tuesday, November 17, 2026 5:41:40 AM

@andrewcaravello
$NWBO #DCVax

?????? ?????????? ?????????? ???????? ???????? ?????? ???????? ?? ?????????? ?????????????? ???? ??????????.

That changes the order of investment.

Northwest could supply an authorized Saudi program from its existing British manufacturing operation while a regional partner establishes access and develops local production.

The company would bring the vaccine, clinical evidence, intellectual property and manufacturing expertise. The partner would bring regional execution and whatever financial commitments the definitive agreement secures.

That is the commercial inflection point to watch: whether assets Northwest has already developed can support international expansion without Northwest having to build and finance every part of it itself.

?????????????? ???? ?????????????? ????????????.

On November 16, Genetix announced that Saudi marketing applications for LYFGENIA and ZYNTEGLO are under SFDA review through SPIMACO.

Both are FDA-approved therapies made from patients’ own blood stem cells.

Genetix announced its SPIMACO agreement on June 23. Confirmation of Saudi review followed 146 days later. The submission dates are undisclosed, so that measures the interval between announcements rather than regulatory review time.

It nevertheless demonstrates execution.

SPIMACO is responsible for authorization and commercialization, with Saudi manufacturing planned. The same company signed Northwest’s August DCVax-L memorandum.

Its operating scale also matters: SAR 1.70 billion in reported 2025 revenue and SAR 184.4 million in net profit, up more than sevenfold. Its SPIMACO Bio subsidiary targets biological, gene and cell therapies.

Northwest’s prospective partner is already doing the regulatory and commercial work contemplated for other individualized cell products.

?????? ???????????????????? ?????????????? ?????? ?????????? ???? ?????? ??????????????.

Northwest’s August 6 MOU proposes a commercial relationship. It is non-binding, with the following division of responsibilities contemplated:

• SPIMACO handles the Saudi application, marketing, sales and distribution.

• Northwest provides the scientific evidence, support and manufactured vaccine.

• Northwest retains its intellectual property.

• Revenue sharing is contemplated, with separate agreements for Saudi manufacturing and technology transfer.

Glioblastoma comes first. Other indications and Gulf territories can follow by mutual agreement.

Then came the regulator-to-regulator agreement.

On November 16, MHRA announced a memorandum with SFDA, signed by Lawrence Tallon and Hisham Aljadhey at the DIA–MHRA summit in London, with Anthony Harnden present.

Its scope expressly includes biologics and advanced therapies. Rare diseases are among its initial priorities.

The company agreement would organize production, payment and distribution. The regulatory agreement establishes a framework for cooperation, information exchange and shared expertise.

A British-manufactured, patient-specific therapy seeking Saudi access sits directly within the kinds of cross-border problems those arrangements are intended to address.

?????????????? ???????? ?????? ?????????????????????????? ??????????????????.

Its other transactions show the commercial model.

Genetix receives technology-transfer payments and a double-digit royalty. Shilpa Biologicals’ agreement includes upfront payments, development and commercial milestones, and product-supply revenue, followed by phased localization.

Those terms belong to those companies. They show what can be negotiated.

For Northwest, the potential value extends beyond supplying individual doses. The ability to reproduce the manufacturing process in another country is itself an asset.

Saudi Arabia has a strong incentive to acquire that capability. King Faisal Specialist Hospital reported that local CAR-T production reduced treatment cost from roughly SAR 1.3 million to SAR 250,000 and manufacturing time from 28 days to 12–14.

Those are CAR-T figures. They explain the economic motivation behind the Kingdom’s investment in advanced manufacturing.

Its National Biotechnology Strategy targets regional leadership by 2030 and global leadership by 2040.

Northwest’s proposed sequence fits that ambition: supply first, then negotiate the transfer of production capability while retaining IP.

?????????????? ???????????????? ?????? ?????????????? ????????.

Sawston received its MHRA commercial manufacturing licence in March 2023. Northwest’s announcement described permissions to export cellular products and import cellular starting materials into Britain.

Northwest acquired Advent, Sawston’s operator, in October 2025. The manufacturing business is now inside Northwest; the building is leased.

An initial Saudi program could connect local collection and treatment to British production, subject to the required product, site, tissue-shipment and import permissions.

Northwest historically estimated capacity of approximately 450–500 patients annually in the first two suites, occupying about 4,400 square feet of an 88,345-square-foot building. That describes potential production capacity, rather than spare slots available for a Saudi program.

Expansion remains a separate issue. Grade C construction began in November 2025, followed by a disclosed pause while engineering continued. The second-quarter filing discussed additional tumor-lysate processing capacity before completion. The latest filing does not establish that the new suite is finished.

On October 26, Northwest announced expansion of its technical team supporting manufacturing scale-up and other priority operations, including restarting U.S. manufacturing.

The distinction is useful: an operating production base can support an initial plan while additional capacity is developed.

???????????????????? ?????????????????? ?????? ???????????? ???????????? ???????????????????? ??????????.

SFDA issued its NADR rare-disease framework on August 5. Northwest announced its MOU on August 6. The framework took effect September 5.

NADR covers qualifying pharmaceutical and biological products, including products still in development. Prior foreign approval is not universally required.

Its designation-assessment target is 20 working days from a complete submission, subject to information requests. A marketing application should follow within six months of designation.

The framework includes rolling submission, conditional approval and natural-history comparators where concurrent controls are infeasible.

For manufacturing sites in listed countries, including Britain, it provides inspection flexibility supported by GMP certificates, the site master file and inspection documentation.

Sawston already has a British regulatory record. Relevant existing documentation could support Saudi assessment without first relocating production.

NADR also permits established platform knowledge and related manufacturing data to support subsequent submissions.

That makes accumulated manufacturing knowledge potentially useful across both territories and future development programs. Each proposed indication still needs an adequate evidence case, but every part of the supporting work need not necessarily begin again.

Regulatory information exchange also remains separate from commercial technology transfer. Cooperation between agencies does not automatically license Northwest’s manufacturing process to another company.

?????? ???????????????? ?????????????? ?????????????? ?????? ??????????????????.

DCVax-L’s published externally controlled survival analysis reported:

• Newly diagnosed glioblastoma: median survival of 19.3 versus 16.5 months.

• Five-year survival: 13.0% versus 5.7%.

• Recurrent glioblastoma: median survival of 13.2 versus 7.8 months.

Subsequent patient-level matching analyses tested the survival finding using individual records from other trials.

SFDA would assess that package. The relevance of NADR is that it provides mechanisms for discussing evidence appropriate to rare diseases and difficult trial settings.

Britain recognized the product’s promise much earlier: DCVax-L received the first UK Promising Innovative Medicine designation in 2014.

?????????????? ???????????????? ?????????????? ?????? ?????????? ??????????????.

Some Saudi routes can be pursued beforehand.

The Breakthrough Medicine Program requires that a product has no foreign marketing authorization when designation is requested. Serious disease, unmet need, potential clinical advantage and benefit–risk must also satisfy SFDA.

The timing of that request therefore matters.

For the complete-data route, the guidance describes approximately 30 working days for designation review, 30 working days to submit the application after designation and a 60-working-day scientific assessment. Information requests affect elapsed time.

Crucially, the guidance permits access negotiations with healthcare entities to proceed alongside application review.

Regulatory assessment and preparation for delivery can move together.

Casgevy demonstrates that the program can accommodate an individualized cell therapy. Its Saudi approval on January 9, 2024 followed British approval by less than two months.

Its logistics are also relevant: collection at an authorized center, specialist manufacturing and return of the product for treatment.

?? ?????????? ???????????? ?????? ???????????? ???????????? ????????????????.

SFDA’s special-access guideline recognizes three alternative eligibility conditions:

• Matching product registration by a listed reference regulator, including MHRA.

• Approval or permission from a reference regulator under the relevant access-program provision.

• A matching product application already under Saudi registration.

A Saudi filing can therefore satisfy an eligibility condition for a separately authorized access program.

Northwest’s existing UK compassionate-use service makes the second route worth clarifying directly with SFDA. The English text refers to permission for the program; the Arabic wording refers to the drug.

British approval would establish the reference-registration alternative while changing eligibility for a new Breakthrough request.

The strategic task is to select and sequence the available routes as regulatory status changes.

The October special-access guideline includes rare-disease requests, a seven-working-day response target and permissions lasting up to 12 months, renewable. Program and import permissions remain necessary.

The applicant funds the program and commits to free product for enrolled patients under the guideline’s conditions.

That makes funding part of the access plan from the outset. Someone must cover manufacture, logistics and care.

?????? ???????????????????? ?????? ?????????????? ?????????? ???? ??????????????????.

DCVax-L requires suitable tumor material and immune cells.

Tumor material must be preserved under the appropriate manufacturing protocol. Routine formalin-fixed pathology material cannot simply substitute. Suitable previously banked material may sometimes be available.

The immune-cell starting material comes from leukapheresis.

NHS Blood and Transplant’s collaboration supports collection and specialist processing. Initial work involves Leeds and Oxford, with expansion being explored across a service operating apheresis units in ten English cities.

NHSBT’s announcement describes the intended scope as glioblastoma “as well as all solid tumours.”

That is a broad development ambition for the platform, with evidence and authorization required for particular uses.

The manufacturing model explains why collection capacity matters so much. Northwest reports approximately eight days of production plus release testing to produce a multi-year set of frozen doses.

A successful collection and manufacturing cycle can support repeated treatment. Each subsequent dose does not require another complete production cycle.

That separates three operational demands: collecting new patients, manufacturing their batches, and storing and administering the resulting doses.

It also supports centralized production with repeated international shipments.

The expense of manufacture is concentrated early. Payment timing is a contractual question; multi-year doses do not automatically mean prepaid revenue.

Saudi Arabia already has relevant infrastructure. King Faisal Specialist Hospital has treated more than 200 CAR-T patients and developed local production. Casgevy has an authorized Saudi treatment-center model.

Apheresis, patient identification, frozen-product handling and specialist administration are established capabilities in the Kingdom.

?????? ???????????????????? ???????????????????? ?????????????? ?????? ??????????????????????.

SPIMACO Bio’s Shilpa agreement covers PD-1 biosimilars. Shilpa’s disclosed development pipeline includes pembrolizumab and nivolumab, although the agreement announcement does not individually identify the licensed molecules.

Pembrolizumab is paired with dendritic-cell vaccination in UCLA’s recurrent-glioblastoma trial and a Pittsburgh ovarian-cancer study listing Northwest as a collaborator.

Northwest’s prospective Saudi partner is building capabilities relevant to both dendritic-cell vaccination and the checkpoint drugs used alongside it.

That provides a commercial and scientific basis for exploring a broader regional cancer-immunotherapy program around the initial DCVax-L collaboration.

???????????????????? ???? ???????????????? ???? ?????? ??????????????’?? ?????????? ????????????????????.

Ruth Jones’s questions 41560 and 41561 seek national brain-tumor preservation standards, retention of suitable surplus tissue and consideration of preservation in the Chalmers review.

Answers are requested for November 17.

NHS England has completed a freezer-capacity gap analysis. Published answers have not supplied a funded rollout timetable or identified all sites receiving additional capacity.

The connection to vaccine access is direct: NHSBT supports the blood-derived input; preservation policy protects the tumor-derived input.

A treatment can become available after surgery. The opportunity to preserve the patient’s tissue may already have passed.

On November 4, Sharon Hodgson raised Braelyn’s case and access to DCVax-L in the Commons. The government committed to urgent examination by the Health Secretary.

The October 14 brain-cancer initiative promised the Chalmers review, a subsequent national action plan and a national clinical lead.

This gives Parliament identifiable implementation questions to pursue: preservation standards, funded infrastructure and responsibility for getting patients through the process.

???????????????? ???????????? ???????????????? ???????????????????? ???????? ????????????????.

Tallon is MHRA’s chief executive and chairs its highest executive decision-making body.

Previously, he was deputy chief executive at Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, overseeing strategy, technology and innovation. His experience includes running healthcare services as well as leading their regulator.

His Saudi relationship predates this summit. SFDA documented a bilateral meeting between Tallon and Aljadhey in October 2025 concerning regulatory cooperation and medicine quality, safety and efficacy.

The new memorandum develops an established relationship.

Tallon has now signed the Saudi agreement and is co-chairing the summit session where Dr. Annalisa Jenkins will deliver a keynote and join the panel.

Northwest appointed Jenkins in April to support its dendritic-cell platform, regulatory strategy and commercialization, explicitly including broader solid tumors and rare cancers.

Her responsibilities overlap closely with the summit’s discussion of investment, policy and international delivery. The programme lists her under The Conscience Collective and Genomics England.

This is a substantive institutional connection. It does not establish a private DCVax decision.

?????? ?????????? ???? ??????????.

November 17 begins with the summit’s advanced-therapy and rare-disease session, involving MHRA, NICE, patient advocates and investors.

The international-regulation session includes Aljadhey and MHRA’s James Pound. The closing plenary begins at 15:15 London time, 10:15 a.m. Eastern, with Tallon co-chairing and Jenkins speaking.

The programme also includes an MHRA parliamentary reception and closing commitments involving the science minister.

The summit is already being used for announcements: the Saudi MOU and MHRA’s Women’s Health Programme. Tallon’s opening recap emphasized faster trials, recruitment and translating science into patient benefit.

Also on November 17 are the requested tissue-preservation answers and a Westminster Hall debate on MHRA performance. Its advertised scope concerns safety, transparency and accountability.

On November 18, Siobhain McDonagh has a PMQs slot. Her supplementary topic has not been published.

The Chalmers review was asked to report within three months of the October 14 announcement. That points to mid-January 2027, approximately January 14 by calendar arithmetic. A separate exact publication date has not been announced. The national action plan follows.

These are opportunities for specific commitments, rather than dates assigned to a DCVax approval.

?????? ???????????????????? ???????? ???? ?????? ?????????????? ?????? ??????????????????????.

Northwest’s November 13 filing still describes negotiations toward a definitive Saudi agreement and continued engagement in the British review. A Saudi DCVax filing has not been publicly verified.

The next agreement becomes consequential through its terms.

Development funding, technology-transfer payments, purchase commitments or funded access arrangements could change how much expansion Northwest must finance from its own balance sheet.

Those commitments have not been disclosed for Northwest. They are what investors should examine when a definitive agreement appears.

The financial stakes are substantial. Northwest reported $725,000 in cash at September 30 and significant current liabilities, while also disclosing a subsequent October financing agreement.

SPIMACO’s resources become useful to Northwest through enforceable obligations: who pays, when payment occurs, who performs the work and what happens if milestones are missed.

An agreement assigning those responsibilities could strengthen Northwest in three ways:

• Share the cost of expansion.

• Put regional execution in the hands of an experienced partner.

• Create income opportunities from existing production, technology and expertise.

That is a more consequential development than another statement of intent.

?????? ???????? ?????????? ?????? ???? ????????????????.

The milestones are a definitive agreement, an appropriate SFDA designation or filing, an authorized access route, named treatment centers and the manufacturing and import arrangements required to deliver doses.

The work can overlap. Regulatory review, access negotiations and preparation of treatment centers can proceed alongside one another where the applicable rules permit.

The regional opportunity also extends beyond Saudi Arabia. Northwest’s MOU allows additional Gulf territories by agreement. SFDA became the first full ICMRA member from the Middle East and North Africa in 2025, and its cooperation with Bahrain includes a 2024 regulatory agreement.

Each jurisdiction retains its own requirements, but Northwest would not be developing regional relationships from nothing.

???????? ?????????????????????????? ???? ????????????.

NHSBT helps organize the route into manufacturing. Northwest brings the technology and production. SPIMACO offers a prospective route into another healthcare system. The MHRA–SFDA agreement gives the regulators a framework for working together.

Each addresses a different part of the same problem: making a personalized treatment deliverable across borders.

The opportunity is to use existing production, retain the value of the intellectual property and develop local manufacturing in stages, with a partner carrying defined responsibilities.

For patients, preparation cannot wait for every institutional decision.

A regulator can authorize treatment later. A company can expand a factory later. Neither can recover a patient’s discarded tumor.

The route begins with suitable tissue and ends with a released dose in a treating physician’s hands.

The decisive next announcement would identify who funds that route, who supplies the vaccine and where patients can receive it. That is the agreement that would turn Northwest’s Saudi opportunity into an operating business.

text:
$KLAR Q3 2026 earnings: Klarna lifts transaction profit, but its plan slows fourth-quarter sales

Klarna is earning more on every dollar shoppers spend in the United States, while growth across its older markets slows. The digital bank and flexible payments provider grew revenue 12% and lifted transaction margin dollars — the revenue kept after processing, funding and credit loss costs — by 32%, beating its own third-quarter plan on every line. Chief executive Sebastian Siemiatkowski kept the full-year outlook unchanged, which leaves fourth-quarter revenue down 2% from a year ago at the middle of the range.

• Revenue (12% excluding currency swings): $𝟏,𝟎𝟎𝟗𝐌 (+12% from a year ago)
• Transaction margin dollars: $𝟑𝟕𝟏𝐌 (+32% from a year ago)
• Operating income, excluding one-offs: $𝟐𝟏𝐌 (-$14M a year ago)
• Full-year outlook: 𝐔𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐝 (revenue $4.08–4.16B; transaction margin $1.62–1.65B)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: ⚪ Neutral

The story is unchanged because passing the third-quarter beat through to an unchanged annual plan leaves the biggest questions for the holiday quarter. On the positive side, Klarna held its full-year transaction profit target even after dropping an accounting change that would have pulled forward about $30 million of gains. The caution: without $53 million of upfront gains from selling loans to outside investors, transaction profit per dollar of payment volume barely budged from a year ago by our math.

The question now is whether the shift to longer US installment loans and paid cards is genuinely lifting lending margins, or whether upfront loan-sale gains are simply pulling future interest income into today's results. If underlying margins are rising, transaction profit will keep outpacing volume without bigger loan sales; if it is timing, interest income will stay flat and profit will track how many loans buyers take. Fourth-quarter loan-sale gains and record required operating profit will tell.

[Model: Gemini 4 Argon. Full article with charts - link in bio]

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐔𝐒 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐭
Klarna is shifting shoppers from short-term interest-free split payments, which it calls Pay Later, to longer interest-bearing installment loans called Fair Financing. Management targets a transaction margin — the revenue kept after processing, funding and credit loss costs — of 3% to 4% of volume on these longer loans, more than triple what Pay Later earns.

• Fair Financing volume: $5.2 billion, up 61% from a year ago and now 15% of total volume
• US Fair Financing volume: $3.6 billion, up 73% and now 43% of all US volume
• Merchants offering Fair Financing: 283,000, up by 27,000 from last quarter
• US transaction margin: 18% of revenue, up from 6% a year ago, lifting US transaction margin dollars past four times last year's level to $70 million

This product shift matters because transaction costs rose just 3% while total payment volume grew 10%. Credit loss provisions fell 6.1 percentage points of revenue and funding costs dropped 1.9 points, which outweighed a 2.2-point rise in payment processing and card costs.

What to watch: US transaction margin as a share of revenue in the fourth quarter. Another step up toward Europe's 49% level would show the older US loan cohorts are paying off as planned.

🟢 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐒𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞
Klarna wants consumers to use its app for everyday spending and paid memberships rather than just occasional checkout loans. Third-quarter volume on the Klarna Card more than doubled from a year ago to $4.5 billion, and 6% of active consumers now use the card, rising to 11% in the United States.

Paying card subscribers tripled from a year ago to 2.6 million. That pushed subscription revenue up more than sixfold to $43 million in the quarter, or $178 million on an annual basis in September. Because members pay recurring fees regardless of how much they shop, this revenue flows straight into transaction profit and softens seasonal swings.

What to watch: paying subscriber additions and card credit losses in the fourth quarter. Klarna noted that financing on the card nudged US installment delinquencies higher, so subscriber fees must keep outpacing those early loan losses.

🟢 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐨𝐫 𝐃𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐬 𝐖𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐌𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐍𝐞𝐭𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤
Klarna expands its store network primarily through "default-on integrations with the world’s largest payment service providers", which turn Klarna on automatically for participating retailers. That rollout lifted total merchants by 59% from a year ago to 1.35 million, with 142,000 net new retailers added in the third quarter alone versus 64,000 a year ago.

In October, Fiserv's Clover platform went live at 100,000 US physical stores, alongside new launches at Southwest Airlines, J. Crew and Marks & Spencer. In addition, Klarna kept its full-year transaction profit target of $1.62 billion to $1.65 billion even after dropping an accounting change that would have pulled forward about $30 million of profit.

What to watch: fourth-quarter payment volume against the implied $42.6 billion to $44.6 billion target. Hitting that range requires a 21% jump from the third quarter as these new payment partners ramp up for holiday shopping.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐅𝐮𝐥𝐥-𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐏𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐋𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐅𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞
"Looking ahead, we’re finishing the year strong as we are running on track with, or ahead of, all our full year outlook," chief executive Sebastian Siemiatkowski said. Third-quarter revenue beat the middle of the company's own target by $49 million, and operating profit excluding one-offs beat by $11 million.

Yet management did not raise the full-year outlook, which squeezes the math for the holiday quarter. The reiterated plan leaves fourth-quarter revenue at $1,017 million to $1,097 million, down 2.3% from a year ago at the middle of the range after growing 12% in the third quarter. At the same time, the plan requires $100 million to $120 million in fourth-quarter operating profit excluding one-offs, above the $91 million record set in the second quarter.

What to watch: fourth-quarter revenue against last year's $1,082 million result. A drop from a year ago would show that slower volume outside the US is weighing on the top line despite the third-quarter beat.

🔴🔴 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧
Klarna sells bundles of consumer loans to outside investors through committed agreements called forward flows. Bulls see this as a capital-light way to recycle cash into new lending, and this quarter the group decided it "no longer expect to sell our US and German Fair Financing loans to the extent that would trigger the fair value through P&L accounting presentation that was flagged in Q2".

• Loans sold in Q3: about $7.7 billion
• Net gains on loan sales in revenue: $53 million, compared with zero a year ago
• Interest income: $273 million, up just 1% from a year ago as sold loans left the balance sheet
• Transaction margin as a share of volume: 1.03% as reported, but 0.88% without loan-sale gains by our math, barely above 0.86% a year ago

Scrapping the accounting switch keeps future loan-sale gains visible on their own line, which helps transparency. However, selling loans pulls revenue forward into the current quarter while giving up future interest income, so almost all of the improvement in transaction profit per dollar of volume still comes from buyer demand for those loans.

What to watch: fourth-quarter net gains on consumer receivables, which Klarna expects to rise from $53 million. If transaction profit grows only by selling a bigger share of the loan book, underlying lending margins are standing still.

🔴 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐆𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐏𝐮𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐝 𝐊𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐚 𝐁𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐚 𝐋𝐨𝐬𝐬
After reporting positive net income in the first two quarters of 2026, Klarna posted a $65 million net loss in the third quarter and a $53 million operating loss. Management pointed to the "timing on higher share-based payments we flagged for the third quarter as part of our annual compensation cycle", which rose 38% from a year ago to $54 million.

Even excluding stock grants and one-offs, operating expenses grew 19% from a year ago to $350 million, outpacing the 12% rise in revenue. General and administrative overhead jumped 43% to $90 million (rising 1.3 percentage points of revenue on a reported basis), while marketing rose 18% to $100 million (also up 1.3 points of revenue) ahead of partner launches.

What to watch: fourth-quarter share-based payments and general overhead. Klarna expects stock compensation to drop back to earlier levels and predicts positive net income in the fourth quarter.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Several standing risks from last quarter received no detailed update in the third-quarter earnings release or data tables.

• German retail volume: volume growth outside the US slowed to 7% from 15% last quarter, and the release did not break out Germany's revenue.
• US Pay Later volume: stood flat from a year ago at $4.52 billion even as US installment loans surged 73%; management did not say whether shoppers are switching products or pulling back.
• US regulatory and legal exposure: no update on the August 2026 Federal Trade Commission draft complaint, the $100 million to $200 million legal liability estimate, or the US bank charter application.
• Executive departures and Apple lease risk: no update on the search for a new finance chief and marketing chief ahead of their early 2027 handover, or on residual device risk in the Apple Upgrade program.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐲 𝐒𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐇𝐚𝐝 𝐋𝐢𝐭𝐭𝐥𝐞 𝐄𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐨𝐧 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝-𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡
Because Klarna earns over 60% of its revenue outside the United States, currency moves often skew its reported dollar results. In the third quarter, currency effects were nearly zero, holding back payment volume and transaction profit growth by 1 percentage point while cutting operating expense growth by 1 point. The full-year outlook assumes benchmark interest rates follow current market curves and sets the euro at $1.12 and the British pound at $1.33.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐀𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐮𝐦𝐞𝐫 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟑𝟒.𝟎  ⇗ accelerating
Revenue per active shopper rose 21% from a year ago to $34.0, up from $33.7 last quarter and $28.1 a year ago. Total active consumers — people who used Klarna or logged into the app in the past year — grew 7% to 122 million, adding 2 million users in the quarter as existing shoppers took on cards and installment loans.

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐮𝐦𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟐,𝟕𝟑𝟑 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇄ reversing
Customer bank deposits rose 9.1% from last quarter to $12.73 billion after falling for three straight quarters, though they remain down 8.9% from a year ago. Deposits supply 88% of Klarna's funding. Total consumer loans on the balance sheet slipped 2.0% from a year ago to $10.00 billion by our math because Klarna sold more loans to outside buyers.

𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐜𝐫𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐭 𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐬 % 𝐨𝐟 𝐆𝐌𝐕 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟎.𝟓𝟔%  ⇒ stable
Credit loss provisions — money set aside for unpaid consumer loans — fell to $201 million, or 0.56% of payment volume, down from 0.72% a year ago "reflecting continued improvements in underwriting and a larger share of loans offloaded". Compared with last quarter's 0.52%, the rate ticked up 0.04 percentage points as seasonal lending and card financing grew.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐦𝐞 (𝐆𝐌𝐕): $𝟏𝟒𝟗.𝟎–𝟏𝟓𝟏.𝟎 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from $149.0–151.0 billion
Unchanged. The full-year plan still calls for about 17.3% payment volume growth at the middle of the range after management cut the target from above $155 billion last quarter. For the fourth quarter, Klarna says this leaves $42.6 billion to $44.6 billion, or 12.7% growth from a year ago and a 20.9% jump from the third quarter as holiday shopping and new payment processors ramp up.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞: $𝟒.𝟎𝟖–𝟒.𝟏𝟔 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 (𝟐.𝟕𝟒–𝟐.𝟕𝟓% 𝐨𝐟 𝐆𝐌𝐕)  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $4.08–4.16 billion (2.74–2.75% of GMV)
Unchanged. The outlook keeps full-year revenue growth at 17.4% at the middle of the range, even though Klarna cancelled the fair-value accounting shift that had lowered reported revenue in the prior forecast. That leaves fourth-quarter revenue at $1,017 million to $1,097 million, a 2.3% drop from last year's $1,082 million at the middle. If the 5.0% four-quarter average beat holds, by our math fourth-quarter revenue would reach $1,110 million.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐓𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐝𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐫𝐬 (𝐓𝐌𝐃): $𝟏.𝟔𝟐–𝟏.𝟔𝟓 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 (𝟏.𝟎𝟗% 𝐨𝐟 𝐆𝐌𝐕)  ⇘ decelerating
🠆 unchanged from $1.62–1.65 billion (1.09% of GMV)
Unchanged. The plan keeps transaction profit growth at 32.0% for the year. Holding this range is an underlying upgrade of about 0.02 percentage points of volume (~$30 million) because the outlook no longer includes the cancelled accounting pull-forward. It leaves fourth-quarter transaction profit at $414 million to $444 million, up 15.3% from a year ago at the middle, slowing from 32.0% growth in the third quarter.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞, 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐨𝐟𝐟𝐬: $𝟐𝟖𝟎–𝟑𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 (𝟔.𝟗–𝟕.𝟐% 𝐨𝐟 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞)  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from $280–300 million (6.9–7.2% of revenue)
Unchanged. Full-year operating profit excluding one-offs is still set to more than quadruple from $65 million in 2025. That leaves $100 million to $120 million for the fourth quarter, or 10.4% of revenue at the middle of the range by our math, requiring the highest quarterly profit in Klarna's history as third-quarter marketing investments pay off and loan-sale gains rise.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐥𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐩𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐭𝐡-𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞?
Dropping the fair-value accounting switch removed a 0.10 percentage-point drag on reported revenue, and the third quarter beat by $49 million. Yet the unchanged full-year plan leaves fourth-quarter revenue down 2.3% from a year ago at the middle of the range.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐆𝐞𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧 𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐦𝐞 𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐫𝐝 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫?
Last quarter management cut its full-year volume outlook partly because of softer German retail spending. Volume growth outside the United States slowed from 15% in the second quarter to 7% in the third, and the release gave no country numbers for Germany.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐮𝐩?
Klarna sold $7.7 billion of loans in the third quarter and booked $53 million in upfront gains, while interest income grew just 1% from a year ago. Investors need the yield and term of the sold loans to judge the trade-off.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐡𝐚𝐬 𝐔𝐒 𝐏𝐚𝐲 𝐋𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐦𝐞 𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠?
US Pay Later volume was flat from a year ago at $4.52 billion after shrinking 2% in the second quarter, even as total US volume rose 24%. Management has not explained whether existing shoppers are moving to installment loans or spending less.

#sapsNC [ZF MGCAWU DISTRICT CELEBRATES 3RD DISTRICT EXCELLENCE AWARDS]

The South African Police Service in the ZF Mgcawu District hosted its 3rd District #ExcellenceAwards on Monday, 16 November 2026, at the Desert Palace Casino in Upington. 

The event recognised and celebrated the outstanding achievements, dedication and commitment of #SAPS employees across the district, including members from various stations, and units under the theme: "Serve with pride, lead with integrity- Strive for Excellence. "

The prestigious annual event was hosted by the ZF Mgcawu District Commissioner, Major General Monica Sebili and attended by the Northern Cape MEC for Transport, Safety and Liaison, Ms Limakatso Koloi,  the Provincial Commissioner, Lieutenant General Koliswa Otola, Deputy Provincial Commissioner for Crime Detection, Major General Luntu Ngubelanga, Deputy Provincial Commissioner for Policing and Acting Deputy Provincial Commissioner for Corporate Services, Major General Johnny Besnaar;  the Pixley Ka Seme District Commissioner, Major General Nomana Mtukushe, the Frances Baard District Commissioner, Major General Charlotte Makgari,  the Namakwa District Commissioner, Brigadier Schalk Andrews and the Acting District Commissioner of John Taolo Gaetsewe District, Brigadier Kenneth Baloyi, Provincial Heads; senior officers; representatives of labour unions SAPU and POPCRU; and provincial and district CPF representatives; and sponsors.

The programme commenced with a scripture reading and prayer by Chaplain MJ Titus followed by a message by Major General Sebili. 

Brigadier Peet Coetzee, the Station Commander of Upington SAPS, delivered the welcoming address and outlined the purpose of the event.

"Excellence is not merely about what we achieve,  but about the dedication,  integrity and courage with which we serve.  Every act of service makes a difference,  every challenge builds character,  and every life we touch strengthens our communities ", cited Brigadier Coetzee. 

The District CPF Chairperson and representatives of Labour Unions, SAPU and POPCRU, delivered messages of support.

 A common message emerged from the addresses: hard work, dedication and teamwork are essential to effective policing, and the contributions of the men and women in blue remain invaluable in ensuring safer communities.

Representatives also acknowledged the commitment and outstanding performance of members. 

In her address, Lieutenant General Otola underscored the importance of recognising and celebrating the outstanding achievements,  dedication and performance of members. 

She acknowledged the vital role played by those serving in the operational and detective environments as well as the indispensable contribution by members in the support environment. 

"When members see that their efforts are noticed and appreciated,  it strengthens morale and inspires them to strive for higher standards," said Lieutenant General Otola

Delivering the keynote address, MEC Koloi acknowledged the sacrifices made by the men and women in blue who ensure that communities are safe. 

She encouraged the members to execute their duties without fear or favour and commended them for their hard work and dedication. 

Awards were presented to officers and members across the administration, visible policing and detective environments in 11 categories. 

Special awards included CPF of the Year, Sportsman of the Year, Man of the Year, Woman of the Year, and Social Crime Coordinator of the Year, recognising exceptional performance, leadership and contributions to policing and community safety.

In recognition of appreciation, the office of the District Commissioner, represented by Brigadier Coetzee, presented a token of appreciation to Lieutenant General Otola, who attended the awards for the final time before her retirement in 2027.
