Culture Wars: Is Wikipedia’s Leo Frank Article Occupied Territory Guarded by Fanatical Hasbara Sentinels?

In my view, the Leo Frank article on Wikipedia is under occupation by Frankites.

What's a Frankite?

By “Frankites,” I mean those multigenerational devotees, who defend Leo Frank's innocence with what I regard as an almost religious fanaticism. I believe some will say or do anything to convince people Leo Frank was innocent or, failing that, to cast doubt on his guilt. Frankites will even openly commit academic fraud, knowing that 99% of their readers will never fact verify their unsupported claims and unsubstantiated assertions.

Over the years, I have challenged what I consider academic fraud in accounts of the case, including stories of antisemitic death threats shouted inside the courtroom that I regard as historical hoaxes. I examine these disputes in my 2025 revised second edition of The Murder of Little Mary Phagan. CP Connolly and Arthur Burton Rascoe have both promoted these hoaxes in print.

My criticism is not that every historian who believes Frank was innocent has engaged in fraud. It is that historians must separate what the original records establish from what they believe those records mean. When an allegation first appears decades after an event, I want to know where it originated and whether anybody checked it against the surviving evidence.

Some problems in Wikipedia's article involve interpretation. Others concern dates, figures, and historical assertions that can be checked against the original records.

The Mary Phagan Bite-Wound Hoax

One of the most questionable stories repeated in pro-Frank books defending Leo Frank concerns alleged bite marks on Mary Phagan's body and photographs supposedly showing that Frank's teeth did not match them.

The legend can be traced to Pierre van Paassen's 1964 autobiography, To Number Our Days. Van Paassen claimed that in 1922, while researching the case at the Fulton County Courthouse, he discovered photographs showing bite marks on Mary's neck and shoulder. He also claimed to have found X-ray photographs of Frank's teeth supposedly demonstrating that Frank could not have inflicted the injuries (van Paassen, 14).

I have spent more than half a century examining the trial record, contemporary newspapers, medical testimony, appeals, and Governor Slaton's commutation proceedings. I have not found a contemporaneous medical report identifying those bite marks, a dental comparison excluding Frank, or the photographs van Paassen claimed to have discovered.

Dr. H. F. Harris, who examined Mary's body on May 5, 1913, testified about the head injury, strangulation, and other findings. His surviving testimony does not identify the bite marks later described by van Paassen (Harris, 13).

Yet Wikipedia states that an analysis of a bite mark on Mary's shoulder helped cast doubt on Conley's testimony (Wiki Con, 4).

What analysis? Conducted by whom? Where are the original photographs, medical reports, and findings?

Van Paassen published his account in 1964, fifty-one years after the murder and forty-two years after he supposedly discovered the photographs. Furthermore, an X-ray of someone's teeth is not the same as a dental impression suitable for comparison with an injury. Modern forensic research has also raised serious questions about the reliability of human bite-mark identification.

Wikipedia does not expressly repeat the supposed dental X-ray story from 1964, but it presents the alleged bite-mark analysis without explaining its uncertain documentary foundation.

Until the original evidence is produced and examined, this should be treated as an unverified allegation, not established forensic proof of innocence.

The Knights of Mary Phagan Hoax

Another disputed claim involves the name “Knights of Mary Phagan.”

The men who abducted and lynched Leo Frank on August 16 and 17, 1915, were identified in contemporary accounts as a vigilance committee. I have not found a contemporary statement from the actual lynching party identifying itself as the Knights of Mary Phagan.

On Saturday, June 26, 1915, approximately seven weeks before Frank's lynching, The New York Times published an article titled “Violence Feared in Atlanta Today.”

The report claimed that approximately 150 citizens had gathered near Mary Phagan's grave in Marietta and formed an oath-bound organization to be called the Knights of Mary Phagan (NYT, 10).

But this was published before the lynching. The newspaper did not establish that the alleged organization's members were the same men who later abducted Frank. 

The reported gathering of 150 people was not a membership list for the approximately twenty-five to thirty men involved in the lynching. Nor have I found evidence that those men publicly identified themselves as Knights of Mary Phagan.

Wikipedia acknowledges the name Vigilance Committee but introduces the Knights of Mary Phagan in its discussion of the Ku Klux Klan's revival as though the organizational connection had been established (Wiki Con, 4).

A newspaper reports the possible formation of an organization in June. Later writers associate that organization with the August lynching. Eventually, the association is repeated so often that readers assume it has been proved.

Where is the contemporary document establishing the connection?

Show me a membership list, a statement from an identified participant, or an organizational declaration.

My family condemns Frank's lynching. We believe in law and order, not vigilantism. But condemning an unlawful killing does not justify attaching an unverified organizational identity to its perpetrators.

The June 1915 report establishes that the name was circulating before the lynching. It does not prove that the lynching party belonged to that organization.

Wikipedia Gets the Ku Klux Klan Revival Timeline Wrong

Wikipedia also states that the Ku Klux Klan's revival occurred one month after Frank was lynched.

That is incorrect.

Frank was lynched on Tuesday, August 17, 1915. William J. Simmons conducted the ceremonial revival of the second Ku Klux Klan at Stone Mountain on Thanksgiving evening, Thursday, November 25, 1915.

That was exactly 100 days later, not one month (Stewart, 11).

The New Georgia Encyclopedia identifies Simmons and his followers as the organizers and discusses the influence of D. W. Griffith's film The Birth of a Nation.

Historians have connected the atmosphere surrounding Frank's trial and lynching to the Klan's revival. That connection deserves examination, but the actual founding date should not be confused with an earlier organization whose connection to the lynchers remains disputed.

This is not a disagreement over a witness's memory. It is a straightforward calendar error.

The Supposed Jewish Exodus From Georgia

Wikipedia claims that following Frank's lynching, approximately half of Georgia's 3,000 Jewish residents left the state (Wiki Con, 4).

Half of 3,000 is 1,500 people.

Where are the population records showing that 1,500 Jewish residents left Georgia because of the lynching?

The Goldring/Woldenberg Institute of Southern Jewish Life reports that Atlanta alone had approximately 4,000 Jewish residents in 1910. Its historical account also reports that Atlanta's Jewish population grew to approximately 12,000 by 1937 (ISJL, 12).

Wikipedia's implied statewide population of 3,000 in 1915 is therefore lower than the independently reported population of Atlanta alone five years earlier.

That discrepancy does not prove nobody left Georgia. Population estimates differ, and people move in both directions. But it requires an explanation.

Steven Hertzberg, in his 1978 study Strangers Within the Gate City, also challenged exaggerated accounts of a general Jewish panic and exodus following the lynching.

I do not dispute that Jewish residents experienced fear or that individual families may have left Georgia. But a claim that half the Jewish population of an entire state departed is measurable. How many left? During which months? Where did they relocate?

If the figure cannot be documented, Wikipedia should correct or qualify it.

The Evidence Against Leo Frank

My strongest objection to Wikipedia's treatment of the criminal case is how frequently it introduces evidence against Frank only to follow it with the defense's preferred explanation.

The article presents the modern historical consensus that Frank was innocent and Jim Conley was probably the murderer as though the central question has been settled. Among its sources are Leonard Dinnerstein, Steve Oney, Jeffrey Melnick, and other authors sympathetic to Frank's innocence.

Their research deserves examination, but modern historical consensus does not establish that Conley committed the murder. Conley was never convicted of killing Mary Phagan.

Frank was convicted by twelve jurors on August 25, 1913. His appeals failed. The Georgia Supreme Court upheld his conviction, and the United States Supreme Court denied federal habeas corpus relief by a vote of seven to two on April 19, 1915.

Those judicial decisions do not eliminate the possibility of a wrongful conviction. Courts can make mistakes. But historians should not confuse their retrospective conclusions with a judicial determination that Conley was the murderer.

I reject the suggestion that Frank was convicted without evidence. The prosecution presented witness testimony, circumstantial evidence, a timeline, and Conley's account of events. The defense disputed much of this material, and the jury evaluated the competing accounts.

Readers should examine the original trial brief of evidence rather than rely entirely on summaries written decades later.

Monteen Stover and the Word “Irrelevant”

Consider Monteen Stover, the young factory worker who testified in July that she waited in Frank's office from 12:05 to 12:10 p.m. on April 26, 1913, and did not see him.

Frank told police that Mary Phagan had entered his office between 12:05 and 12:10 p.m., perhaps around 12:07. That statement appears in State's Exhibit B (State of Georgia, 7).

Stover's testimony therefore raised an obvious question about Frank's whereabouts during those five minutes.

Wikipedia acknowledges the conflicting accounts but calls Stover's testimony and its implications “irrelevant,” relying on a reconstruction of Mary's streetcar journey and estimated arrival time (Wiki Con, 4).

Irrelevant according to whom?

The streetcar witnesses did not all give identical times. The reconstruction depends on estimates of walking time and the time needed to enter the building and reach Frank's office.

Why should one defense interpretation of the trolley evidence automatically eliminate the conflict between Stover's testimony and Frank's original statement?

Newt Lee and the Murder Notes

Newt Lee, the Black night watchman who discovered Mary's body, became an early suspect. Three items raised questions about him: the murder notes found near Mary's body that implicate Lee, the manufactured gaps in his time card, and the blood-smeared shirt discovered at his residence.

The prosecution contended that Frank had attempted to direct suspicion toward Lee. The defense maintained that Conley independently wrote the murder notes and that Lee knew more about the murder than what he was telling.

Conley admitted writing them but testified that Frank dictated their contents to frame Newt Lee.

These were central questions at trial. Yet Wikipedia's narrative encourages the conclusion that Conley was the murderer.

Readers should examine Conley's original testimony, the detectives' accounts, and the defense's objections. They should also investigate how Frank's explanation of Lee's time card changed during the investigation.

The original questions and answers deserve more attention than the conclusions later pro-Frank authors drew from them.

The 1986 Pardon Was Not an Exoneration

On March 11, 1986, the Georgia State Board of Pardons and Paroles granted Frank a posthumous pardon.

The board expressly declined to determine guilt or innocence. Its decision recognized Georgia's failure to protect Frank from lynching and to bring his killers to justice. The board had rejected an earlier pardon application in 1983 because it could not conclusively determine guilt or innocence (Georgia Board, 8).

Wikipedia acknowledges these limitations later in the article, but its introduction describes Frank as wrongly convicted. The Wikipedia article presents a lopsided defense team version of the case, the prosecution gets little hearing. The evidence against Frank gets little hearing.

These are different conclusions. One reflects the prevailing interpretation among modern historians. The other concerns the actual legal scope of the pardon.

The pardon did not establish that Conley was the murderer or that Frank was innocent. The pardon did not vacate Frank's conviction. 

Readers should understand that from the beginning.

Wikipedia Founding Father Larry Sanger and Decentralization

Larry Sanger deserves credit for helping establish an encyclopedia that anybody could contribute to.

Jimmy Wales and Sanger launched Wikipedia on Monday, January 15, 2001. Ordinary people could share knowledge, correct mistakes, and make information freely available worldwide.

My understanding of that mission was decentralization, not control by small groups of politically committed editors.

On July 8, 2026, Sanger wrote that Wikipedia was ruled by “a few hundred anonymous demagogues who dominate the rest.” He argued that powerful editors could use vague rules and administrative authority to exclude views they opposed (Sanger, 1).

I believe the Leo Frank article illustrates some of his concerns.

There have also been actual classes teaching people how to influence Wikipedia.

In August 2010, My Israel, working with the Yesha Council, conducted a seminar in Jerusalem called “Zionist Editing for Wikipedia.” Experienced editors taught volunteers how to contribute to articles in ways intended to improve Israel's public image (Baruch, 2).

On August 18, 2010, Israel National News, also called Arutz Sheva, published a video report documenting the event (Arutz Sheva, 6).

Ayelet Shaked of My Israel explained that even the terminology describing Ariel in the West Bank could become an editorial contest. Naftali Bennett, then director of the Yesha Council, said the organizers wanted to present their side (Shabi, 3).

I have not established that anyone involved in those workshops edited the Leo Frank article, and such a connection should not be asserted without evidence.

But the workshops demonstrate that political organizations have deliberately trained volunteers to influence Wikipedia's wording.

That is why readers should examine an article's edit history rather than assume that every statement appearing under Wikipedia's name is impartial.

Read What Wikipedia's Editors Said About My Work

The public discussion page attached to the Leo Frank article is worth reading.

On July 8, 2026, an editor wrote, “Phagan-Kean is not an expert.” Other participants questioned whether my book qualified as a reliable historical source. On July 14, another editor asked critics to identify qualified modern historians who considered Frank guilty (Wiki Con, 5).

Well, I began visiting public libraries in Georgia with my mother and father in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

I read books on the case and compared their accounts with original newspaper reports and legal records. When an author told me what a witness said, I wanted to know whether that was what the witness actually said.

Sometimes the very next question changed how I understood the answer.

I have spent more than half a century studying the Mary Phagan case, especially Leo Frank's trial and appeals. To my knowledge, few authors have spent more years examining the surviving records.

Yet an anonymous Wikipedia editor can dismiss my work without identifying a single factual error in the passage being challenged.

If I have quoted a witness incorrectly, tell me the witness, date, page number, and what the source actually says. I will examine it.

My book and my understanding of the case remain works in progress, even after fifty years of research.

I made numerous changes to my 2025 revised second edition compared with the 1987 publication. I invite readers to compare them. The original edition is available online for free, without registration, at https://t.co/J3I52F2XEP

I am not asking anybody to accept my conclusions because of the number of years I have studied the case. I am asking that claims be judged against the original evidence.

That applies to my research just as much as it applies to Dinnerstein, Oney, Melnick, Frey, or anybody else.

The Leo Frank Wikipedia Challenge

An anonymous writer once recommended what I call the Leo Frank Wikipedia Challenge. Every year I invite people who believe the article gives the prosecution a fair hearing to try it.

Open a Wikipedia account under an ordinary username. Spend two years contributing to articles on subjects you know. Learn the rules, study the policies concerning reliable sources, make several hundred legitimate contributions, and recognize when another editor raises a fair objection.

Then study the 1913 trial evidence, newspaper reports, appellate decisions, and modern historical works. Go to the Leo Frank article and propose a carefully documented correction that challenges its prevailing interpretation.

Start with “irrelevant” in the discussion of Monteen Stover. Or ask the editors to explain the evidence behind the alleged bite-mark analysis, the Knights of Mary Phagan identification, or the Jewish population exodus.

The Klan-revival timeline offers an especially straightforward test. Replace the claim that the revival occurred one month after the lynching with the documented date, November 25, 1915.

Put your correction on the Talk page with the source and page number. If rejected, examine the editor's explanation and the evidence used to justify it.

Keep a record of the exchange. Wikipedia's revision histories and discussions are public.

I believe you may discover why I describe the article as occupied territory.

But do not take my word for it. See for yourself.

An Invitation to Future Historians

I would also like to invite university students, especially those who already hold bachelor's degrees and are considering graduate study, to consider pursuing a Ph.D. in history.

The Mary Phagan case offers serious research opportunities in legal history, Southern history, journalism, antigentilism, public memory, and the development of historical narratives over generations.

I invite students to help examine the original evidence, publish articles, and write books that challenge inaccurate accounts of the past.

Do not simply repeat my conclusions. Question everybody's conclusions, including mine. Examine the prosecution and defense with equal care.

If a source contradicts something I have written, bring it forward.

I want a new generation of historians who understand how to read trial transcripts, trace claims to their earliest appearance, compare newspaper accounts, and distinguish evidence from interpretation.

Consider what ten or twenty trained historians could accomplish over the next thirty years with access to an organized archive containing the surviving records.

We need independent research, books grounded in primary sources, and opportunities for readers to examine the evidence without depending on one encyclopedia or one group of authors.

We must take back our history through scholarship, not by replacing one unquestionable narrative with another.

The Mary Phagan-Kean Legacy Project

My family has been fighting for more than a century to set the record straight about what happened to little Mary Phagan.

Today, the Mary Phagan-Kean Legacy Project is bringing that work to a worldwide audience.

My team and I have transcribed more than 2,200 newspaper articles published between 1913 and 1915, principally from the Atlanta press, together with thousands of pages of legal records and historical documents.

These records cover the investigation, coroner's inquest, grand jury proceedings, murder trial, appeals, commutation, and aftermath of Frank's lynching.

They are the same kinds of records I began searching for with my mother and father in Georgia libraries during the late 1960s and early 1970s.

Back then, much of the material existed only in bound newspaper volumes, on microfilm, or in difficult-to-obtain legal collections. Researching one question might require several library visits and hours of searching.

Now we can distribute the records electronically.

Over the coming years, I intend to make these transcriptions available through X and other online platforms so present and future generations can examine the original material themselves.

We are also producing thousands of audio recordings, historical newspaper-clipping videos, and lip-sync presentations recreating the words preserved in contemporary sources.

People throughout the world can now read the same newspaper reports, examine the same trial testimony, and compare the original records with books published decades later.

We no longer need to depend entirely on a small number of authors to understand what was reported during the original investigation and trial.

I want students to build dissertations from these records. I want historians to challenge established interpretations. I want readers to identify errors in my work if they can document them.

And I want those defending Frank's innocence to examine the entire prosecution record rather than dismiss it through a few familiar quotations.

Our family does not condone violence, lynching, or vigilantism. We believe in law and order.

The reckoning I am calling for is historical and scholarly. It belongs in archives, books, journal articles, classrooms, public debates, and documented corrections to the historical record.

For more than a century, arguments over Leo Frank have often overshadowed the life and murder of Mary Phagan herself.

I intend to keep her at the center of this work.

The original sources belong to history, not to any political organization, institution, author, or Wikipedia editor.

Our family's struggle to preserve this history has lasted more than a century. I want the work we are doing today to continue for generations.

We will take back our history, one original document at a time.

Hung Cao: Senator, thank you for that question. Again, the original place that we, the original abandoned National Guard facility was not adequate for safety and security of our people. So that's why we turned down that area. I think we're working, I believe we're working together to look for a secondary place. I mean, there's, again, the Reserve Center is very important. One of my former commanding officers commanded that Reserve Center many years ago, and again, it brings the Midwest together. And so we are committed to working with you in order to find a more adequate place to move that Reserve Center, sir.

Schmitt: Okay. I think we've found that place. So I really want to work with you on that because these things tend to take way too much time. So I wanted to make sure we had a chance to address that. What else in your view would the Navy need from Congress to allow that transfer to occur? Again, Senator, we just need to assess, we need to do a force protection assessment to make sure it's the right place to go, that it's the right facility for all the reservists in that general area to convey to you, and then I will come back to you and work with you to get Congress to, if we need any legislation or any kind of verbiage from Congress in order to make that move happen, sir. Okay. All right. Well, we'll follow up with that. As relates to readiness along with modernization, the Navy's moving forward with the next generation fighter. We're going to be guiding the FAXX, and that will be built, coincidentally, in St. Louis. We're very happy about that. I just wanted to ask you with the time that I have, what are your plans as far as sort of funding moving forward for that? The Air Force has their F-47, the Navy now has their FAXX, how are you thinking about funding to make sure that that's adequately resourced and on time?

Hung Cao: Senator, again, I was speaking to this with Ranking Member Reed yesterday in terms of we still have to fly the F-35 until late 2040s. Just like right now, we're still flying the FA-18 until the foreseeable future, and so FAXX, I'm glad that we're able to partner with the Air Force, being the same company that's building F-47 is going to build the FAXX, and with that, we're able to learn a lot from the Air Force to accelerate the FAXX program. As of right now, we literally just awarded the contract a little over a month ago. We're doing the preliminary decisions to see how much it would cost in order to get the low rate initial product out there so that we can accelerate the program and get the next generation fighter. We need this for our near-peer competitors and our peer competitors if we go into a fight with China or Russia. Can we get you out to the 1.1 million square foot facility where they're going to be building it? We'd love to have you there. By the way, interestingly, it's only about two football fields away from that current installation that we want to move to Jefferson Barracks, so we can do it all in one day. It'll be great. It sounds like a date, Senator.

Schmitt: All right, thanks. Thank you.

Wicker: Thank you very much, Senator Schmitt.

Duckworth: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. I have some prepared remarks, but I just want to start off and reject what my colleagues on the other side of the aisle is saying about Democrats on this side of the aisle, about us wanting to surrender. Let me tell you something. I am a war fighter. I spent two decades, over two decades as a war fighter. I am married to a man who spent three decades as a war fighter. I am the daughter of a gentleman who served during two wars. My daughter is named for great Aunt Pearl, who was an army nurse who kept a pistol in her bra even as she served and even as she treated German POWs on multiple crossings across the Atlantic while being hunted down by German submarines. So let me tell you something. This is about you becoming Navy Secretary, and are you going to stand up for the men and women in uniform? And the question is not about whether or not we're going to let the Iranians control the Strait of Hormuz. They didn't control the Strait of Hormuz before this ill-thought-out war. Now we've given them veto power over the Strait of Hormuz that they did not have before Trump, the five-time draft-dodging coward, decided to launch this war. So let's be clear. Someone who did lead troops, unlike our Secretary of Defense, who, by the way, managed to make it to the rank of major without a ranger tab, jump wings, or an air assault badge, or a company command, the most unqualified Secretary of Defense in this nation's history, someone who had more experience than that Secretary of Defense, did you or did you not stand up to this Secretary and say, "Mr. Secretary, I do not think that moving forward is going to be in the best interest of the readiness of our nation's Navy"? Did you stand up to him and tell him that it was time to bring our troops home?

Kelly: Secretary Cao, thank you for your appearance and your service here today. We've heard a lot from Democratic senators this morning about ending the Iran war, by which I think they mean surrendering to Iran, just simply unilaterally raising the white flag, letting Iran control the Strait of Hormuz, letting its terrorist proxies control other critical waterways in the region, letting them rebuild their nuclear weapons program as well. I, too, would like to end the Iran war by winning the war. I wish we had won it in April by allowing the military to finish its operational plan and then put in place the blockade that we've had in place over the last few months and by forcing the Strait open, as it has been now for a couple months. We need a victory strategy, not an exit strategy. We certainly don't need another ill-advised, naive, foolish memorandum of understanding, which this summer allowed Iran to regroup and rearm and enrich itself and probably prolong the war. We've heard complaints about forever wars. It's probably that memorandum of understanding that allowed the Democrats to characterize this conflict as a forever war. We need to end it by winning it now. But since our Democratic colleagues keep talking about ending the war, let me ask you this. If we took that approach and simply surrendered and raised the white flag and allowed Iran to control the Strait of Hormuz and its terrorist proxies to run the entire region, would the Navy's need for the budget it's requested be any different at all? If we stopped everything we're doing with the blockade and the Strait of Hormuz today, would the Navy be able to reduce its budget request by a single penny?

Hung Cao: Senator, thank you very much for that question. Again, let's go back to the Iran issue. I mean, this has been going on for 47 years. All the IEDs that I stopped in Iraq and Afghanistan, in fact, I'll tell you right now, one of the caches I found is in the Maison Valley in a small boat that have these EFP liners that explicitly form penetrators. We downloaded the GPS and it went right back to Iran. Those came from Iran. They were killing and maiming our soldiers and soldier-sailors, airmen, Marines in Afghanistan and Iraq for decades. In fact, one of the families, Sean Levi English, his son told me when I was running for office that, "Sir, when you win, please make sure the Iranians pay for taking my father away from me." And so these are things that, look, they've been killing and maiming our people for years. But the budget that we submitted to the Congress was before Epic Fury started. This is what we need. This is the generational change we need in order to rebuild our fleet from 20 years of war in Iraq and Afghanistan. So even if we surrendered in Iran, as the Democrats apparently propose, the Navy would still need all of this money to rebuild its munition stockpile, to continue on its shipbuilding plan and to protect the nation from threats like communist China or Russia or other terrorist groups. Senator, you're absolutely right because what we're dealing with now is stuff that happened from 20, 25 years ago when we stopped building ships. I mean, again, we need to be able to build like we did back in World War II. This is why I say this is our 1939 moment, Senator.

Kelly: Thank you. Another claim we've heard from the Democrats is substandard conditions on ships, especially ships on extended deployments. Those are always serious matters that need to be thoroughly reviewed by the chain of command. If you've had anything along those lines, I would expect the chain of command to take appropriate action up to and including yourself. I have confidence in you and the Navy to do so. If the picture painted by the Democrats were so bleak, would the Navy have reached its recruiting goals three months early, as I understand you did, with 45,000 new recruits?

Hung Cao: Senator, we would not be there, and in fact, I'm glad you brought that up. The retention rate on board USS Abraham Lincoln throughout this deployment was 84.4% retention rate. That is above any carrier out there. Well, I'm glad the Navy is doing so well in recruiting and retaining sailors for the future.

Kelly: Thank you.

Hung Cao: Senator Cotton, I completely agree and subscribe to the statement you made before your first question, and I thank you for pointing that out.

Wicker: Senator Shaheen.

Shaheen: Thank you, Mr. Chairman and Acting Secretary Cao. Thank you for being here. Secretary Cao, I was also moved by your very amazing personal story. I very much appreciate the service that you and your family have provided to this country, but I have to be honest and tell you I have serious questions about your decision making, about your willingness to stand up to your superiors and make clear your views and that they should be listened to, and about your ability to be transparent with Congress. You said that you think submarines are the apex predator, and I certainly agree with that, but we can't rebuild our shipping industry by hamstringing our public shipyards, and during your last testimony in May, I asked you about the $65 million budget shortfalls that are facing the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard. At the end of 2025, you required installations to give bonuses to top performing, in quotes, civilian employees, and you did that without providing the additional funds. That forced Portsmouth to take $32 million out of its operations and maintenance budget. You also pulled back another $33 million from the shipyard for under execution of hiring, which doesn't make any sense because they were prevented from hiring workers by the personnel office and by the department until Congress stepped in and exempted them from the civilian hiring freeze. This shortfall has had a real tangible impact on the ability of the shipyard to do its job. Your office response when we raised these issues provided no commitment or path forward to mitigate this, that you even acknowledged that there is, and I'm quoting, there's a real impact to Virginia class submarine availabilities, specifically the USS Virginia and the USS South Dakota. So why was there no budgeting for a hiring thaw? Why was there no acknowledgement that the shipyard would be unable to hire on schedule because of the freeze that had been put on by the administration? And how can you now hold the shipyard accountable for that and refuse the $65 million budget shot shortfall that they need?

Hung Cao: Senator, thank you for that question. Again, I came in the shop in April 22nd of 2026 and so I, and I know that in May when we, I'd just taken over and we did the posture hearings, you asked me about this and I'm going to tell you right now that I failed you. I was supposed to bring you back the answers and I didn't do that and I commit to you right now that with within a week of us, us finishing this, I will find out the answer and we will, we will find them a way to work together and again, if confirmed, I will work with you to make sure that we free up the $33 million in order to, to, to, to adequately pay for that. Well, acting secretary Cao, you have heard from a number of members of this committee on both sides of the aisle, our frustration with the lack of transparency from the department that we are not getting information that's requested and that people are disassembling when they're asked direct questions.

Shaheen: Have you been instructed by secretary Hegseth or anyone else within the department to not be open with Congress when you are asked questions that are difficult to answer?

Hung Cao: Senator, I do not know the daily cost, ma'am. You don't have any idea? You've been running this thing since April and you don't have any idea what that costs? Well, Senator, I know the rough costs, how much it's costing us so far. But again, the cost of losing the Strait is even worse. I'm not asking you that. I just want to have the dollars here. Divided estimates are about thirty two point five million dollars a day. Does that sound about right to you, Senator? And let me do some quick Asian math in my head, but yes, it's about three thirty billion dollars. OK, so you you confirm that number. And that means the American taxpayers are spending about a billion dollars a month just on this blockade. Let's do another Iranian strikes have also caused extensive damage to U.S. bases and facilities in the region, including the U.S. naval base in Bahrain. It's home to U.S. Naval Forces Central Command and the U.S. Fifth Fleet and is a critical strategic hub for the U.S. military. You yourself said that Iran, quote, blew the hell out of that base. But the Navy has yet to tell Congress or the American people how much that damage costs. So acting secretary, Cao, when Iran hit our naval base in Bahrain, how much did that cost? Well, Senator, we have not been able to do a full assessment yet because it's still not a full assessment. What's your estimate? Senator, it's again, we're still making all the the assessments because it's a non permissive area for us to go. So no number until I pull a number from somebody else. In June, The Wall Street Journal estimated that the damage to the U.S. naval base in Bahrain has cost the United States at least 400 million dollars. That's a lot of money. It's not included in the Pentagon's estimates for the cost of this war. Does that number sound about right to you? Senator, I'll find out. You've been running this for more than half a year and you don't even know if this is in the right area? Senator, I can't again, we have to assess the damage and we still have to go in there. You're just now thinking of assessing the damage in November. So look, Trump's war is costing taxpayers billions. It is harming our readiness all while driving up prices here at home. So it's no surprise that the Trump administration doesn't want to reveal the total cost of this war. The Pentagon has admitted that it's at least 47 billion dollars already, 47 billion dollars and counting, all while Republicans have slashed health care for millions of Americans. This is outrageous. We should not spend another cent on this war and instead we should be spending this money at home to lower costs. So let's do a little math, Acting Secretary Cao. How many Americans federal student loans could we wipe out with the 47 billion dollars that we have already spent on this war? Senator, I, if we didn't have a blockade, we would, we already protected 3700 ships. Did you hear my question? Senator, we, we, I'm asking you for the 47 billion dollars that we have already spent on this blockade. I'll tell you the number. It's more than 2 million people could have all their student loan debt wiped out. For an extra 47 billion dollars we could send every four year old in America to a high quality pre-K for a year. For an extra 47 billion dollars we could knock about 200 dollars a month off the monthly insurance bill for families with private insurance. For an extra 47 billion dollars a year we could wipe out unpayable medical debts for more than 10 million families and instead the Trump administration has signed Americans up for another forever war that America didn't want. Congress should use all of our tools at our disposal including the upcoming government funding bill next month to end this war and end it now.

Wicker: Thank you, Senator Warren, Senator Banks.

Banks: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Secretary Cao, thank you for being here. Congratulations on your nomination. Can you talk for a brief moment about why it's important to, not just to you, but to our sailors why we have a permanent confirmed Secretary of the Navy instead of an acting secretary?

Hung Cao: Senator, thank you very much for that question. By statute I can stay in this job until the president fires me or until January 20th, 2029. But not having a permanent person into this billet means that every six months I have to rotate out with the undersecretary of the Navy because they're PTDO performing the duties of and so they're limited to 210 days of work.

Banks: And then not only that, it doesn't give the steady hand that the Navy needs in order to negotiate with industry. They're going to see me as a temporary guy even though I would be there until the president fires me or until January 20th, 2029, Senator. Why does that matter to the sailors?

Hung Cao: To the sailors, they need a steady hand, Senator. They need to see a Secretary of the Navy that's leading them, that understands, that's been there with them in the trenches and that's why they... What authorities does a confirmed secretary have that an acting secretary doesn't have? Well, Senator, as the acting, again, I have everything under statute to do my job, but again it's the negotiating with industry that's going to be hard because they only see me as an acting person and so a temporary guy, I'm not able to get the better deal for our taxpayers. Well, I'm here because I think it's fundamentally important that we have a confirmed Secretary of the Navy for the next two years and we got to get you confirmed.

Banks: I want to thank you for coming to Indiana just a few weeks ago. You have, even in both of your roles, you have shown more interest in Crane Navy Base than any Secretary of the Navy before you and I greatly appreciate that, not just because I represent it, but because of the important role that it plays to our nation's defense. I really appreciate that more than anybody else, you made something happen that makes Crane bigger, better, more influential than it's ever been before in bringing the one star position, the Program Management Office to Crane. Admiral Finney arrived at the beginning of October, as you know, to lead the PMO and I wondered if you could elaborate just for a moment on the strategic importance of that move and why it matters to the Navy.

Hung Cao: Senator, I'm so glad we were able to work together to get the Admiral up there because this is going to accelerate our SLICM-N as well as hypersonics. So SLICM-N is, I mean, imagine not just having 14 ballistic missile submarines out there that have nuclear weapons, but also the other 55 submarine fast attacks and Virginia payload modules that the Virginia class summaries, the SSGNs also that will be able to launch nuclear missiles and that helps with deterrence. And so the Admiral going up there will be able to work between the office down here and all your engineers up there in Crane to accelerate the SLICM-N program, to accelerate hypersonics. Imagine a weapon that can go from here to California in 17 minutes and that's what the hypersonics can do from ships or submarines that can't be seen anywhere. And that's exactly why we need to accelerate these weapons systems and these programs and no better place than Crane, Indiana.

Banks: Thank you for that. I know the Navy's initial plan is for at least 150 government civilians to join the Admiral by the end of FY 29. I just wonder about that. Is the commitment still there from the Navy that this end strength will represent a floor, not a ceiling for the PMO?

text:
6/21
Blumenthal: Thanks, Mr. Chairman. From up north. I'm not going to get into this contention. Mr. Cao, Secretary Cao, the world is less safe as a result of the Iran war. We've seen costs soar, lives lost, casualties, our relationships with allies deteriorate as a result of this war. In fact, the Navy has been stretched beyond sustainable limits under your watch and the fleet is in worse condition than it was when you took office along with this president. The USS Abraham Lincoln's deployment in particular, just one example, raises serious questions about your leadership of the Navy and even more important, your candor to members of this committee. The Lincoln was supposed to sail on a seven month deployment. Instead, the carrier was deployed, as you know, nearly 11 months, including 265 days, consecutively without a port call. Now, the USS George Bush was supposed to be home, but you told families just last week that there was no end in sight to their deployment and that the Bush will come home when Iran agrees "to a non-nuclear Iran." You're all familiar with the shortages of food, basic supplies, water contamination, broken plumbing, deteriorating living conditions, disruption in mail delivery, and serious mental health concerns on the Lincoln and now seemingly on the Bush. You're failing these sailors and their families and your confrontation with them leaves me with the clear impression that you simply don't care. But equally important, you failed to provide Congress with a full and transparent accounting of the toll on these sailors and their family. Just last August, I wrote to you and demanded answers about the situation on that ship, the Lincoln. You responded my inquiries on sailors' mental health by saying the strike group had "not seen a statistically significant increase in serious mental medical emergencies." Only later did you acknowledge eight suicide attempts across the carrier strike group. I directly asked you about the health and welfare of sailors aboard the Lincoln. Why did you withhold critical information to me and other members of this committee?

Hung Cao: Senator, I appreciate your concern on all these issues.

Blumenthal: Let me first address the fact that you said that I don't care.

Hung Cao: Senator, I look at everything through one lens and one lens only. How will this affect my son, a United States Marine, all his fellow Marines, and his shipmates? That's the vision that I look through, the lens I look through, every decision I make. And so I care greatly for our sailors. They know ... Your solution seems to be to continue just asking these sailors and their families for more without giving them or us the truth about what the nature and length of their deployment is going to be. Well, Senator, I don't control the deployment lengths, but I did re-answer those inquiries right away, especially with the mental health issues. You see as eight suicide attempts, I see eight suicides mitigations because of the chaplains we have on board, the deployment resiliency counselors as well as mental health specialists. Normally, most carrier strike groups, when they deploy, have about one or two suicides. This is well before Epic Fury, before all this stuff. It's just, unfortunately, this is the fight we're dealing with right now. We had zero actual suicides on board the Abraham Lincoln. I equate that to the ... Again, the chaplains, the mental health providers as well as the deployment resiliency counselors.

Blumenthal: Let me just move on because I know my colleagues will have questions on this topic as well. There are reports that one of the tankers potentially carrying illegal diesel oil as a result of the president's deal with Vladimir Putin may dock at a naval port. This sale would be illegal if it occurs and the diesel is offloaded at a naval facility. Will you commit to this committee that the Navy will never allow sanctioned Russian fuel or any other illegal good to be offloaded in any of its facilities?

Hung Cao: Senator, we will abide by law to the fullest extent. I will look into this situation. I am not aware of it, but I will look into this, but again, the Navy and Marine Corps will abide by all laws. Well, I will take that as a commitment that it will not be allowed to offload. The Fernandez, which is the name of the tanker, currently, apparently is within range of that port potentially in Virginia. I will take that as a commitment that you will not allow that diesel to be offloaded at a naval facility.

Blumenthal: Is that correct?

Hung Cao: Senator, if confirmed, I will ensure that we abide by every single letter of the law.

Blumenthal: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Mr. Secretary, will you respond also on the record to that last question?

Hung Cao: Yes, Chairman, I will answer on the record when I find out the answers.

Blumenthal: Okay. And when did your, how long has your son been a Marine?

Hung Cao: Senator, he was commissioned in May. And where is he now? He is down in Quantico training in the field right now. Well, thank you very much.

Wicker: Senator Rounds.

Rounds: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Secretary Cao, first of all, thank you for joining us today and for your continued service to our nation. I enjoyed our conversation in my office and appreciate your efforts to work with Congress to address matters of critical importance to our Navy and to our national security. I want to begin with one specific question because I think it's one that will come up during your tenure, and that has to do with spectrum issues, electromagnetic spectrum issues. It's one that I continue to focus on. As we discussed in my office, I've long been concerned about protecting military capabilities which require use of the electromagnetic spectrum, particularly in the lower 3 gigahertz band. With Word Radio Communication Conference 2027 approaching, we're also looking closely at X band, specifically the 7.4 to 8.4 gigahertz range. Can you share which Navy systems rely on these frequencies and what the operational consequences would be if the Navy were forced to vacate or significantly restrict its use of that portion of the spectrum?

text:
The City of Franklin is pleased to announce the selection of Cris Randall as the City of Franklin’s next Director of Human Resources and Risk Management. Randall will officially join the City on January 11, 2027.

Randall currently serves as the Human Resources Director for the City of Alpharetta, Georgia. Her career also includes service as the Human Resources Director for the City of DeKalb, Illinois, and as Management Services Director for the Algonquin-Lake in the Hills Fire Protection District in northern Illinois. She has led broad portfolios that include employee and labor relations, benefits and retirement administration, workers’ compensation, safety and risk management, talent acquisition and retention, and classification and compensation.

“Cris emerged as the top candidate from a field of approximately 100 candidates through our national search and stood out for her leadership and collaborative approach,” stated Kristine Brock, Assistant City Administrator for Finance and Administration.  “I’m grateful to our HR team for their work during this process and look forward to welcoming Cris in January.”

Randall earned a Master of Public Administration from Northern Illinois University and a bachelor’s degree in Justice Studies, with an emphasis in Human Resource Management, from Fort Hays State University. She holds the Certified Public Manager (CPM), Certified Labor Relations Professional (CLRP), Professional in Human Resources (PHR), and SHRM Certified Professional (SHRM-CP) credentials. Her professional recognition includes the James Baird Leadership Award from the Illinois Public Employer Labor Relations Association and the National Public Employer Labor Relations Association Pacesetter Award for excellence in developing and delivering supervisory skills training.

“Cris greatly impressed us with her experience, talent, enthusiasm, and passion for public service and for supporting public servants,” said City Administrator Eric Stuckey. “Our employees are central to the quality of service Franklin provides to residents, and Cris’s commitment to supporting them aligns well with our values.”

“I am truly honored and excited to join the City of Franklin,” shared Randall. “I believe great communities are built by people who care deeply about serving others. I look forward to getting to know the Franklin team, building meaningful relationships, and working alongside the HR and Risk Management teams and City leadership to support our employees and build on the strong foundation already in place.”

text:
If you really want $STRC and other digital credit products to be able to attract hundreds of billions, if not TRILLIONS, of capital through their products in the future, you need it to be a product that can attract that volume of capital.

That wont happen if the company allows it to sit at $90-95 for 6-12 months whist they 'wait' for the market to move it. 

Institutions with hundreds of billions of dollars to invest want security first. The rate of return is secondary.

Most people on X speak as if its the other way around.

Institutions want assurances that if they allocate $50B of capital into $STRC, they'll not only receive their 12% return, but they'll also not wake up one morning & see that their $50B of shares is now only worth $40B & they'll have to 'wait 6 months for the market to push it back up'. 

It's @saylor's and @phongle's job to engineer. construct and manage the product accordingly to ensure that those two things happen. 

Action over passiveness. It's that simple. 

If they can consistently demonstrate that confidence to institutions (over multiple years, not days or months!), the amount of capital they'll be able to attract will continue to grow.

Buybacks offer the best defence to keep it pegged to par.  

It sends a message to the market that getting STRC to par is a priority and they're going to defend it relentlessly. That gives confidence to larger investors that their invested capital is 'safe'.

I see people complaining that Strategy have diluted the common shareholder in recent months and they could have simply increased the rate and waited for it to return to par.

They complain that Strategy have spent $2.6B on STRC buybacks, but don't consider that by doing so and providing confidence to institutions that they are prepared to defend it and keep it close to par, that it could open up the door to 10 institutions all committing to invest $5B to STRC.

Passiveness over action. Hope over action.

The ultimate goal should be to be an issuer at $100.01 and a buyer below $100 and to peg it to par indefinitely.

There's $300T of capital in the fixed income market. I want Strategy to get as much of the capital through STRC over the next decade. 

They wont get there unless they can keep STRC pegged to par. 

Their action this year are laying the foundations for them to build over the next 20-50 years. 

Think ₿igger.

Changelog v1.2.0

New:
• Google phone checks in a Bot's message show a Google verification card with a QR code to scan or open on your phone. Requires Grok Bot 1.1.0 or later.
• Team admins can turn off Proactive messages for the team's Bots from the dashboard. (Teams)
• Connectors that use your organization's single sign-on connect with Sign in with SSO, and your browser returns you to the Bot afterward. (Enterprise)
• Hotel photos open in a full-size viewer with the hotel name, a photo counter, thumbnails, and previous and next buttons.
• Hotel and place maps have Zoom in and Zoom out buttons, the Location map can be dragged and recentered, and hotel pages add Copy address.
• In the expanded Mermaid diagram view, right-click and choose Copy Image to copy the diagram as a PNG.

Improved:
• Flight results are redesigned: select a flight to see Full details and Book, or expand it for bags, changes, and refund rules.
• Flight searches show their steps, such as Searching flights and Checking the fare, and Book buttons hide while the Bot books that flight.
• When no flights match your airline, departure time, or stop filters, the Bot shows the closest options and says which filters it relaxed.
• The Tasks page groups Done, Canceled, and Archived tasks into one Closed section, with filters for each and search.
• On the Tasks page, click a task's files pill to list its files and open any of them, and task tags show as colored pills.
• Follow-ups, corrections, and repeats of tracked work continue the existing task and build on its earlier results instead of starting over.
• When the Bot rewrites a Page you have open, a New updates available pill loads the latest version at your scroll position.
• Clicking Update closes the dialog at once, the sidebar shows checking, download, and preparing progress, and Grok Bot restarts when ready.
• Take over and End call on a live phone call card ask you to confirm first, so a misclick no longer ends or transfers the call.
• Command approval cards show the exact command in full with hidden characters marked, and Allow once runs it one time only.
• Opening a prompt link asks you to confirm before it fills a Bot's chat box, and links with suspicious hidden characters are blocked.
• Open a Bot in its own window with New window in its right-click menu; double-clicking a sidebar row no longer pops it out.
• In Quick Chat, the element you pick stays highlighted in your Bot's color, and on macOS the Bot also sees the page title, address, and highlighted text.
• Product pages show up to four options per group with Show all, and About and Reviews sections with the rating and review count.
• Hotel pages show the review score with stars and the review count, the Website detail opens the hotel's site, and the map lists hotels beside it.
• Hotel and car rental results show the search radius in miles or kilometers to match your computer's settings.
• Shopping cards leave out products without a real photo when others have one, and a card with no photos arrives as a text list.
• Order tracking checks more often as delivery gets closer, up to hourly once a package is out for delivery.
• Before showing an order card, the Bot settles checkout contact details such as the receipt email, so payment doesn't stall after you tap Pay.
• When a sign-in page offers only a QR code to scan, the Bot sends you its link to tap instead.
• Auto-review decides on large and binary file writes on the Bot's computer, so safe ones go through without an approval card.
• The Bot's remote browser starts several seconds faster when it carries over your sign-ins, cookies, and open tabs.
• Automations that control the desktop type and respond much faster, matching interactive computer use.
• In meetings, the Bot picks up your answer to its question, or the rest of your request, said within a minute without its name.
• Asking the Bot to share a Project returns the Project's page and says who can join: the team, invitees only, or only its owner.
• When you're added to a Team Bot, its intro message can mention its role, its owner, and which team accounts it uses. (Teams)
• MCP tools you turn off for a server in your desktop MCP settings are also hidden and refused in your own Grok Bot turns, including routines.
• Flight searches check fares from more sources, so results come back more reliably with comparison options.
• Connector controls read Sign In, Sign In Again, and Sign Out, and apps that run locally say Runs on your computer after you sign in.
• On a team Bot, people who can use but not edit the Bot can click its skills in chat to view them read-only. (Teams)
• Unconnected plugins in the @ menu show just the plugin name and a Connect action.
• HTML file previews run without network access, so remote scripts, stylesheets, fonts, and images no longer load.
• Large Excel workbooks show their first rows right away while the rest of the sheet loads.
• The sidebar resize handle can be focused with Tab and resized with the arrow keys, Home, and End.
• Team admins manage Grok Bot network mode, allowed destinations, and team blocked sites from Security, beside the organization's blocked sites. (Teams)
• Group MCP allowlist imports show whether each rule applies Local only, Cloud only, or Local and Cloud, and ask you to confirm each surface's first rule. (Teams)
• The Setup column for customer-hosted computers shows each computer's team setup script status, with revisions and failure details on hover. (Enterprise)
• Team setup scripts set to run outside the guest container receive the team's Team Secrets and setup files. (Teams)
• When context sync is off, a Project's Notes page and Library say Context sync is not running instead of a generic loading error.

Fixed:
• Chat uploads over 25 MB, including videos, reach the Bot's computer so it can open and work with them.
• The Bot stops computer tasks stuck repeating the same clicks, and a hung click, keystroke, or wait stops after 30 seconds and tries something else.
• Computer use clicks land on their target instead of drifting up and to the left.
• Browser and screenshot tools wake the Bot's sleeping computer instead of refusing.
• Browser and desktop tasks no longer stop with a model not offered in your region error; the Bot switches to an available model.
• Hotel searches show bookable rooms and rates for hotels that previously said their rooms couldn't be shown.
• When a store doesn't accept your card's brand, the Bot offers a new order card with an accepted payment option instead of stopping.
• When X Money card payments aren't enabled for your account, the Bot says so and offers the same order with another payment method.
• Shopping and product cards appear reliably, including when the reply also links a product, and order and shipment cards appear in their task's thread.
• The Bot reliably notices when a checkout declines your card or asks for it again, and uses your own email for receipts and order updates.
• Approving a purchase card while the Bot replaces it no longer shows the new card as expired, and the replaced card shows as expired.
• Card numbers, expiry dates, and security codes are removed from memories, including long ones, team memory, Bots shared as templates, and forget requests held for review.
• Before filling a saved login, the Bot opens the site's sign-in page, and a fill that stalls stops after two minutes.
• When filling a form you answered, the Bot checks the open tab, so a crafted page address can't send your answers to another site.
• Connectors linked through your own account work in your private Grok Bot chats instead of showing as not connected.
• Connected apps no longer disappear for hours after a brief outage, and your MCP tools stay available when the server list briefly can't be read.
• Changes to your team's MCP allowlist and connector settings take effect right away, including after you add, edit, or remove a skill. (Teams)
• On Slack and X Chat, replies about a connector or plugin your team admin blocked name it and say it's disabled by your admin. (Teams)
• When a team admin has turned MCP servers off, the Bot refuses adding one right away instead of showing an approval card first. (Teams)
• Group MCP rules that list no servers keep the team's MCP servers, and Local only or Cloud only rules keep team servers allowed for Grok Bot. (Teams)
• In Slack, a shared Bot's sign-in link for a team-added connector opens a working sign-in page. (Teams)
• Skill links in replies on Slack and Teams show as their plain name instead of raw link text.
• A Grok Bot running on a team's own computer no longer picks up skills from the owner's personal computer. (Teams)
• An email to your Bot's inbox wakes a bot on that inbox's team, never one from another team.
• Grok Bot can read and upload SharePoint files in chats with no team selected.
• Meeting notes no longer get dropped when they take longer than 45 seconds to write.
• Transferring a Grok Bot's ownership completes reliably and pauses the previous owner's routines.
• Routines finish running their code before reporting back, and a routine deleted elsewhere is reported as already deleted.
• Work handed to another of your bots no longer leaves a task stuck in For Review.
• The Bot recovers when its code checker times out or a server hiccups mid-task, instead of ending with the work undone.
• A connector tool with a self-referencing input schema no longer stops the Bot from using your other connector tools.
• Asking for a usage breakdown of more than 20 bots or routines lists the top 20 with a note instead of failing.
• Publishing a skill to your team refuses links and unreadable files in its folder and names the entry to fix. (Teams)
• With a proxy set on the Bot's computer, healthy windows no longer restart, and taking over to sign in brings the open page forward.
• Editing a Page with the Bot keeps its summary, link preview card, live data, and visualizations, and printing or saving it as PDF includes the whole Page.
• The consent page for connecting an outside app to Grok Bot loads reliably for users with many bots.
• Grok Bot no longer says your phone isn't connected when the device status check is slow or the app is briefly in the background.
• The Test Setup Scripts panel in team settings masks Team Secrets and setup file URLs that scripts print. (Teams)
• Clicking Update installs the newest build, including when a newer version is downloading or a restart for an update failed on macOS.
• When a monthly spend limit blocks sends after buying credits, the banner stays visible and offers Increase limit.
• The Messages connector reads chats on macOS 14 and earlier, and older Macs say they need macOS 14 or later.
• The plugins dialog loads plugin status and skills for people on several teams, and plugins your admin disabled hide their Setup section.
• Signing out on desktop switches you to your other saved account instead of showing the sign-in screen.
• Connectors that need a data center before sign-in show a connect card where you pick it, and Connect shows Connecting… until you're signed in.
• Connectors on the From Grok shelf in Connect Apps show their logos and their server's host.
• Read-only tools in the built-in pull request connector count as reads, so Read-only bots can use them.
• Inline MCP App cards fill the conversation width and expand to their full height, so tall widgets are no longer cut off.
• Hotel photos load reliably, and hotel, car rental, and place pages scroll every tile and room card into view and let you select text.
• After a declined or cancelled flight booking, the trip card shows Book again, and expired cheaper fares no longer show a Book for button.
• Clicking a link inside a Page opens it in your browser, even on Pages with draggable strips or carousels.
• Pressing Enter twice quickly on a Search result opens it without sending the draft in the Prompt.
• Closing menus, dialogs, and panels with Escape returns keyboard focus to where you were, and dialogs open with focus on their first field.
• Keyboard shortcuts in a popped-out chat act on that window, and shortcuts no longer change the chat behind an open dialog.
• On Linux, the title bar Minimize, Maximize, and Close buttons work while a dialog that can't be dismissed is open.
• The Thinking indicator stays on a running turn after a reload or relaunch, and shows when a credit grant pays for the reply.
• The Tasks list and the chat header agree on which tasks are working, scrolling fast no longer shows blank rows, and long task titles truncate.
• A Bot profile's Routines section no longer gets stuck on Loading…, and a saved time zone that isn't valid no longer breaks it.
• Webhook routines on shared team Bots explain that only the owner can get the URL and key, or that team settings block personal API keys. (Teams)
• A teammate's new or shared bot no longer flashes in your own bot list in the sidebar and tray. (Teams)
• A skill name after @ in a reply, such as @pack-for-rain, links to the skill, and prompt links no longer fill a message box.
• Searching the Ctrl+K palette for emoji or symbols finds Bots and Pages with them in their names.
• Link preview cards close when you click outside or scroll, and checklists in chat match the spacing of other lists.
• Changing the language keeps Settings open on the same section, and onboarding fits small windows.
• Plugin account names over 255 characters show the limit inline, and the avatar editor no longer errors when the Bot's computer is unreachable.

text:
Toronto won the JuJu lottery. The fit works, and the contract makes it even better.

At No. 1, JuJu’s rookie deal is $2.53M over 4 years. Year 1 is $565,000.

That would make her the 3rd-highest salary on the roster, behind Mabrey ($1.2M) and Sykes ($1.19M). The best player on the team would make less than two of her teammates.

Why the fit works on the floor:

-Allemand is a pass-first PG who doesn’t need the ball. JuJu can run the offense from the wing while Allemand handles the ball up the floor and spots up.
-Nurse, Mabrey and Allemand can all shoot. Put 3 of them around her and the help defender has to choose: take away JuJu’s drive or stay home on a shooter.
-Sykes and JuJu would give Toronto two long perimeter defenders who can switch 1 through 3 and jump passing lanes.
-Morrow does the rebounding and dirty work. She doesn’t need plays called for her, and that’s exactly the kind of big you want next to a high-usage wing.

Where it gets tricky:

-Usage. Mabrey and Rice are both at their best with the ball. If I’m the staff, I stagger them so one is always running the second unit while JuJu sits.
-Spacing. 3-point shooting was never JuJu’s strength at USC (don't get me wrong she can shoot tho) . That makes the shooters around her non-negotiable.
-Her load. People will expect managed minutes after a torn ACL, but I’m not sure that happens. She already played 38 minutes against (No. 1) South Carolina and scored 25. If her minutes go up once conference play starts, Toronto is getting a full-workload star in year one, not a player on a minutes limit.

The cap math:

Toronto has about $3.84M committed for 2027 against an $8.25M cap. With JuJu added, that leaves about $3.85M in space.

About $3.2M of that is already going to 4 guards. Every free agency dollar should go to the frontcourt, and the center market is thin.

The window:

Mabrey and Sykes hit free agency after 2027. JuJu will still be on her rookie deal. The new CBA also lets rookie-scale stars renegotiate their 4th year up to max money, so her cheap years won’t last forever.

That gives Toronto about 2 years to build the roster around her while she’s this cheap.

Who starts next to her: Mabrey or Rice?

text:
Look at what is happening at Arsenal. This is bigger than just signing new contracts; this is a statement of intent. The club is building something special, and the best part is that we are nowhere near our ceiling yet.

- Declan Rice has signed a new deal.
- David Raya is set to sign a new deal.
- Jurrien Timber is set to sign a new deal.
- Martin Ødegaard is set to sign a new deal.
- Gabriel Magalhães has signed a new deal.
- Piero Hincapié is set to sign a new deal.
- William Saliba is contracted until 2030.
- Bukayo Saka has signed a new deal.
- Ezri Konsa just joined Arsenal.
- Bruno Guimarães just  joined.
- There are also reports that Riccardo Calafiori is close to signing a longer contract.

And let's not forget that Mikel Arteta and his coaching staff have also committed their futures to the project.

Just take a moment to understand what this means. Arsenal are not simply building a team for the next season; they are building a squad capable of dominating for years. We are securing our best players, protecting the core of the team, adding quality and ensuring that the people responsible for this transformation remain in place.

This is what long-term planning looks like. This is what stability looks like. This is what happens when a club has a clear vision and everyone is moving in the same direction.

The frightening thing is that this project is still evolving. Arteta is building a team that can compete at the highest level consistently, not just for one season but for many years.

We have gone from rebuilding to competing, and now the focus is on establishing a dynasty.

The foundation is being secured, the future is being protected, and the ambition is clear.

Arsenal are building something that could define an era. The project is approaching its peak, and I genuinely believe the best is yet to come.

25 years ago, I co-wrote this article with Lee Kaplan. Reviewing it today, I see what has changed, & what feels sadly familiar about the conflict between Israel and Hamas in Gaza today.  -- BJ 

"Most Asked Questions about the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict"

By Becky Johnson & Lee Kaplan
   August 12, 2002
 Published by:   https://t.co/OfrpmsKaAN

-- Didn't Israel drive out 600,000 Palestinians at gunpoint in 1948 and take their land?

Most Arabs who left Israel did so under the orders of the Arab leader, the Grand Mufti, to withdraw and let the Arab armies "drive the Jews into the sea," which they attempted in 1948. However Israel won that war. Not all of the Arabs left, and Israel is now 18% Arab. These Arabs have full citizenship rights, can own property, vote, and have 14 representatives in the Knesset, the Israeli Parliament.

-- I've heard that some Israelis say there is no such thing as Palestinians. How can they say that?

Up until the 1967 war, the Arabs living in Israel did not even call themselves Palestinians -- twenty years after the founding of the modern state of Israel. The name Palestine came from the Romans who destroyed the Jewish Temple in Jerusalem in 70 AD. To humiliate the Jews, the Romans renamed the land Palestine after their mortal enemies, the Philistines. The modern land of Palestine was given that name by the British when they took control over from the crumbling Ottoman Empire. In British Palestine, both Jews and Arabs were Palestinians.
