🗞️17 November 2026 | Daily Edition: US Close

Fifteen Minutes Undid the Morning, $64,000 Became the Ceiling

A US strike on Iran and a run of outages knocked Bitcoin through every morning support, while the World Bank picked USDC, Brevan Howard tripled its IBIT stake and the CFTC froze Kalshi's Trump bets.

Prepared around 4:10 PM EST on Tuesday 17 November. This is the full crypto wrap of the US session. It picks up from this morning's First Hour, prepared at 10:40 AM EST, and only adds what happened since. Crypto prices are live prints as of about 4:05 PM EST. Stock figures are 4:00 PM EST closing prints, not yet final official closes. Treasury, dollar and gold figures are live prints from about 4:00 PM EST, not settlement, and the oil figures are the official 2:30 PM EST settlements. Tuesday's spot ETF flows were not yet published at writing.

1⃣ Bitcoin lost $64,000 in fifteen minutes, then could not get back above it

Bitcoin was near $64,750 at the First Hour edition. Between 10:40 and 10:55 AM EST it fell about 2.3% to a low of $63,257 at 10:50 AM EST, cutting through the $64,460 post-open low, this morning's $64,000 to $64,080 lows and Sunday's $63,725 early low. The drop came as reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and an outage of a classified US security network crossed, and as stock losses deepened. A bounce to $64,417 at 11:05 AM EST faded into a retest at $63,377 at 11:55 AM EST. Every low since then has been higher, $63,518 at 12:30 PM EST, $63,544 at 2:35 PM EST, $63,584 at 3:00 PM EST and about $63,770 at 3:50 PM EST, but every high stopped at the same place: $64,052 at 12:05 PM EST, $64,027 at 1:25 PM EST, $64,022 at 3:25 PM EST and $64,023 at 4:00 PM EST. It trades near $63,930, about 1.3% below the First Hour edition and about 1.6% to 2% lower over 24 hours. Today's range is $63,257 to $65,383.

🖊️ Market significance: The opening rejection at the $65,315 weekly close turned into a full reversal. Price is now below every support level from this morning except Saturday night's $61,950 low.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Higher lows under a flat $64,000 to $64,050 lid is compression, not recovery. I need that lid back before I treat the afternoon as repair, and a break of $63,257 puts the weekend low in play.

2⃣ Ether broke $1,772 on the drop but recovered faster than Bitcoin

Ether fell from about $1,799 at the First Hour edition to $1,749 at 10:50 AM EST, through Monday's $1,785 low and the $1,772 level, but stayed well above $1,709. It retested $1,765 at 11:55 AM EST, reached $1,803.50 at 1:25 PM EST, dipped to $1,790 at 3:50 PM EST and pushed to its afternoon high of $1,807 at 4:00 PM EST. It trades near $1,801, roughly flat against the First Hour edition and about 1% to 1.5% lower over 24 hours. Solana dipped to $70.93 at 10:50 AM EST, made its afternoon high of $73.29 at 4:00 PM EST and trades near $73.10, up about 2% to 2.5% over 24 hours. XRP is near $0.969 after a $0.945 low, Zcash is near $922 to $928, below this morning's $936, and HYPE is near $68.30.

🖊️ Market significance: Ether is up about 3% from its low, Bitcoin only about 1%. This time Ether led the rebound instead of lagging it.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Ether is back above $1,800, but only just, and $1,807 is the first test overnight. Solana's steadiness during its own conference week is the cleanest relative strength among the majors.

3⃣ Longs left Bitcoin perps, on-chain traders turned to Nvidia and Anthropic

Bitcoin open interest on the largest on-chain perps venue fell about 1.6% since this morning to about 37,550 BTC, and on a large offshore exchange it fell about 1.1% to about 31,220 BTC, while price fell about 1.3%. Ether open interest rose about 1.9% on the on-chain venue to about 617,500 ETH but fell about 2.0% offshore to about 665,000 ETH. Bitcoin funding is still slightly positive, about +0.001% to +0.009% per eight hours, and Ether funding is mixed, slightly negative offshore and slightly positive on-chain. On the same on-chain venue, the synthetic Nvidia perpetual traded about $565 million over 24 hours ahead of tonight's results, and the Anthropic pre-IPO perpetual traded about $73 million, a record for the contract, with about $140 million of open interest at a mark near $96.20. Neither contract carries any share rights.

🖊️ Market significance: Falling open interest into a falling price means longs closed. It is the mirror image of this morning's short covering at the open.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Leverage came out without a funding spike, so neither side looks crowded tonight. The more telling number is where speculative money went: into AI exposure on crypto rails, not into Bitcoin.

4⃣ The on-chain map now puts the line at $62,000

An on-chain analytics firm's report, published Tuesday, said buyers absorbed about 66,000 BTC between $62,000 and $66,000, that most leverage has been flushed out, and that short-term holders bought very few coins below $62,000. It flagged a cluster of leveraged long positions between about $59,500 and $62,200. A daily close below $62,000 could open a fast move toward the June low of $58,500 and the realized price, the average price at which every coin last moved, of $53,700. A move back above $74,100, the short-term holder cost basis, would confirm a bottom. The report also noted stablecoin supply down 4.2% over 90 days and the US exchange premium back at a small discount, while options traders price roughly a one-in-three chance that Bitcoin settles below $53,700 at the September 2027 expiry.

🖊️ Market significance: Today's $63,257 low sits inside the absorption zone and above the long cluster, so the support that matters has not been tested yet.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The long cluster under $62,200 is the trapdoor. If $62,000 goes on a daily close, forced selling does the work, which is why I treat $61,950 as the line rather than a target.

5⃣ Brevan Howard tripled its IBIT stake, Abu Dhabi's funds held every share

Brevan Howard's third-quarter 13F lists 22,405,494 IBIT shares at 30 September, worth about $1.06 billion, up about 211% from about 7.2 million in June, with separate options positions excluded. Mubadala held 14,721,917 IBIT shares, about $697 million, unchanged for a third straight quarter, and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council held 8,218,712 shares, about $389 million, also unchanged. IBIT is now about 54% of the Council's reported US portfolio after it cut its holdings from 26 issuers to eight. Tudor Investment reported about 1.4 million IBIT shares, about $65 million, roughly three times its June position. IBIT shares fell about 1.8% today.

🖊️ Market significance: After Monday's bank filings, Tuesday's batch adds a macro hedge fund adding size and two Gulf state investors that did not sell a share through the quarter.

🗨️ My viewpoint: These are 30 September snapshots, taken with Bitcoin near $83,500, and Bitcoin is about 24% lower today. The unchanged Abu Dhabi share counts matter more to me than the dollar values, because they show allocation behaviour, not trading.

6⃣ The World Bank will test USDC for development payouts, Western Union opened its Solana network

The World Bank Group said it will explore regulated dollar stablecoins with Citi and Circle, using Citi's banking connections and Circle's infrastructure to mint and settle disbursements in USDC alongside its current correspondent banking setup. It builds on FundsChain, the bank's blockchain ledger that already tracks more than 350 projects in 96 countries. It is an exploration, not a launch, and will start with borrower countries that permit digital assets. Separately, Western Union said its digital asset network is live, so exchanges and wallets can integrate its USDPT stablecoin on Solana for cash payouts, although its consumer site still lists global cash-out as coming soon.

🖊️ Market significance: A multilateral lender is now testing a public stablecoin for its own payment plumbing, a different tier of adoption from fintech pilots.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This lands in a week when stablecoin supply is still shrinking. Institutional use cases are growing while speculative balances leave, and over time that changes what stablecoin supply measures.

7⃣ Coinbase finished its 50-state rollout of on-chain loans

Coinbase Borrow is now available in New York after approval from the state's financial regulator, completing its rollout across all 50 US states. New York residents can borrow USDC against Bitcoin, Ether and Solana held on Coinbase, up to $5 million against Bitcoin, $1 million against Ether and $100,000 against Solana, with Morpho providing the lending markets on Base. Since its January 2025 launch, the product has originated more than $3.4 billion in loans, with more than $1.7 billion outstanding against more than $3.2 billion of collateral, according to Morpho. Fixed-rate loans and other collateral, including tokenized gold, ZEC, HYPE and XRP, are not yet available in the state.

🖊️ Market significance: The strictest state regulator signed off on a retail lending product that runs on a public DeFi protocol.

🗨️ My viewpoint: $1.7 billion outstanding against $3.2 billion of collateral is a conservative book, but it is also forced selling waiting at lower prices if Bitcoin keeps sliding. I watch liquidation activity on Base if $62,000 breaks.

8⃣ Anchorage let institutions use bank-custodied Bitcoin as margin at Kalshi

Anchorage Digital and Kalshi Prime launched a tri-party setup that lets institutions post Bitcoin and stablecoins held at Anchorage Digital Bank as margin for Kalshi Prime's perpetual futures and prediction markets. Anchorage keeps custody of the pledged assets while Kalshi Prime recognises them as margin, so clients trade without moving or selling their holdings. Anchorage's chief executive described it as "no wire, no sale, and no change of custodian". The structure relies on earlier CFTC guidance allowing Bitcoin, Ether and USDC as derivatives collateral.

🖊️ Market significance: Collateral that stays at a federally chartered bank while backing positions on a regulated venue removes one of the main reasons institutions kept crypto idle.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Together with yesterday's custody-backed lending news, the pattern is clear: custody, credit and trading are being separated, the reverse of the 2022 model that failed.

9⃣ Waller wants the Fed's payment rails at the centre of tokenization

Fed Governor Christopher Waller told a banking conference in New York that traditional rails, including large-value and instant payment systems, should remain "a reliable backbone for final funds settlement" on which tokenized markets can develop. He said tokenization and AI agents "could be catalysts for one another". He also cited the $6.3 billion Binance hack and asked who bears responsibility when smart contracts are exploited, private keys are compromised or assets are stranded on failed chains, and said important transactions may need more private and controlled blockchain systems.

🖊️ Market significance: The most crypto-friendly Fed governor is backing tokenization, but on terms where central bank money stays the settlement asset.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The Binance reference matters. When a Fed governor uses a crypto hack to argue for permissioned settlement, public chains have to win the security argument, not just the speed argument.

1⃣0⃣ Tokenized stocks crossed $10 billion on one network as senators pushed back

Broker Alpaca said its instant tokenization network has passed $10 billion of cumulative minting and redemption volume in just over a year, excluding secondary trading, and that it holds more than 90% of the custody market for shares backing tokenized stocks sold outside the US. Its clients can now mint tokens through the DTCC tokenization service that went live on 28 October. In Washington, four Democratic senators, Angela Alsobrooks, Catherine Cortez Masto, Mark Warner and Ruben Gallego, released a letter on Monday asking SEC Chair Paul Atkins 13 questions about the tokenized stock exemption. They said it sets no identity-verification standard, requires no anti-money laundering program and allows tokens to move to unverified wallets, and noted that more than 60 public companies have objected to having their shares tokenized.

🖊️ Market significance: Tokenized equities are scaling fast, and the political fight is moving from whether they should exist to who polices them once they leave a regulated venue.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The exemption runs to 2031, but the letter sets up the next fight. If token-level transfer limits become mandatory, the open, composable version of tokenized stocks gets much narrower.

1⃣1⃣ The CFTC froze Kalshi's Trump bets and set its 24/7 trading agenda

Kalshi confirmed it is complying with a CFTC order to stop listing contracts on what President Trump will say. The halt is for a manipulation review, not a ban on all mention markets, and Kalshi has until 11 December to defend the contracts. The CFTC also published the agenda for its 15 December roundtable on 24/7 derivatives trading, which includes whether tokenization and stablecoins can solve weekend margin and clearing problems. At this afternoon's Senate Agriculture Committee hearing, nominee Matthew Rowland said he wants to restore staffing after the disruption of 2025.

🖊️ Market significance: On the same day, the regulator restricted the most controversial prediction market contracts and opened a formal debate on round-the-clock clearing with crypto collateral.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This CFTC is permissive on infrastructure and strict on contracts that invite insider trading. That is a workable line for crypto, but bad news for mention markets.

1⃣2⃣ A Base protocol lost $404,540, a Solana builder told the industry to slow down

An attacker drained 404,540 USDC from B18TimeBank on Base in one transaction by redeeming signed reward vouchers, according to a blockchain security firm, with about 106,785 USDC left in the settlement contract at a later check and containment unconfirmed. The pattern points to reusable signatures, the same class of weakness as Monday's reused nonces at Lighter. At the Solana conference in London, Jito Labs chief executive Lucas Bruder said builders need to "slow down a little bit" and fix technical debt over the next two years as attackers use AI tools, and said Jito is hiring two more security staff.

🖊️ Market significance: The loss is small, but signature handling is the common thread in this week's incidents.

🗨️ My viewpoint: A founder calling for slower shipping in public is rare. With Waller citing the Binance hack the same day, security is becoming the price of admission for institutional money.

1⃣3⃣ Strategy fell almost four times as hard as Bitcoin

At the 4:00 PM EST close, not yet final, Strategy fell about 6.3% to about $96.50, Circle about 5.2%, Coinbase about 4.0%, Robinhood about 4.0%, MARA about 3.3% and BitMine about 2.5%. Bitcoin is down about 1.7% from Monday's 4:00 PM EST print. ARK's Monday trade file showed it bought about $40 million of Block, Circle and Coinbase shares during Monday's selloff while selling about $85 million of Nvidia, so ARK bought ahead of today's second leg lower.

🖊️ Market significance: Strategy's drop is almost four times Bitcoin's. Investors are cutting leveraged equity exposure to Bitcoin faster than Bitcoin itself.

🗨️ My viewpoint: When the leveraged proxies fall harder than the coin, the stress sits in equity holders, not crypto holders. I watch Strategy's premium and funding plans as Bitcoin approaches $62,000.

1⃣4⃣ The Dow lost about 850 points into Nvidia's results

At the 4:00 PM EST close, not yet final, the S&P 500 fell about 1.0% to about 7,341, the Nasdaq Composite about 0.7% to about 24,328, and the Dow about 1.6%, or about 849 points, to about 50,759. Stocks trimmed losses in the final minutes. Nvidia closed about 0.5% lower, near $155.40, ahead of its results after the bell, its first report without Jensen Huang as chief executive. Huang said he would be "honored" to return if the board asked, while the board is not considering it for now. Apple said outages across several of its services came from an internal update, not a cyberattack, and Charles Schwab's website was reported down for part of the day.

🖊️ Market significance: The Dow fell harder than the Nasdaq, so today's selling went beyond the AI trade into the broader market.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Nvidia's numbers decide tonight's risk mood. A relief rally in tech would help crypto at the margin, but Bitcoin has not shown it can rise on its own this week.

1⃣5⃣ The US struck Iran's Qeshm Island, Williams said there is no case for dramatic action

US fighter aircraft struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island, which Washington called self-defence after attacks targeting US personnel and assets. Iran's navy later said another vessel hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, and a senior source said US and Iran diplomacy has not reached a breakthrough. New York Fed President John Williams said inflation is stubbornly high and the Fed has more work to do, but that the situation does not call for dramatic policy action. Norway's Equinor confirmed a cyberattack on some IT systems with no impact on production, while the Director of National Intelligence said he does not see the day's US outages as a cyber attack.

🖊️ Market significance: Military escalation in the Strait of Hormuz returned during US trading hours, and the Fed's number three leaned against a large hike.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Williams pushes back against this morning's call for several hikes, which helps at the margin. The direct US strike is a new step, and it adds risk to every weekend and overnight session.

1⃣6⃣ Oil settled higher, yields slipped, the dollar and gold were flat

Brent settled up 0.76% at $93.14 and WTI up 0.34% at $86.01, after Middle East tanker attacks and the Qeshm strike. At about 4:00 PM EST, the 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.10% to 5.11%, about 1.5 to 2 basis points lower, the dollar index was near 103.5, roughly flat, and gold futures were near $3,850, also roughly flat.

🖊️ Market significance: Higher oil and a near-flat 10-year above 5% kept financial conditions tight on a risk-off day.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Yields barely fell on a 1.6% Dow decline and a military strike. That says the inflation worry is stronger than the safety bid, which is not a helpful backdrop for crypto.

🗨️ My Overall Viewpoint:
The afternoon confirmed what the open suggested. The third failure at the $65,315 weekly close was followed by a fast break of every morning support, and Bitcoin spent the rest of the day making higher lows under a $64,000 to $64,050 ceiling. Positioning reset: longs closed and funding stayed calm, so there is no forced selling left from today, but there is also no new demand. Ether's 3% recovery from $1,749 was the one bright spot. Under the price, the build-out continued at a high level: the World Bank chose USDC for a payments test, Brevan Howard and Abu Dhabi's funds showed size and patience in IBIT, Coinbase completed its 50-state lending rollout, Anchorage and Kalshi linked bank custody to margin, and Alpaca passed $10 billion in tokenization volume. The policy signals were mixed: Waller backs tokenization but on central bank rails, Democratic senators want tighter tokenized stock rules, and the CFTC froze Kalshi's Trump contracts. text:
Peter Obi Meets US Lawmakers, Calls for Credible Elections, Stronger Democratic Institutions

The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has met with members of the United States Congress and other influential American figures in Washington, DC, where he called for accountable leadership, stronger democratic institutions and credible elections in Nigeria.

Obi disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, November 17, following a series of engagements with members of the US House of Representatives and Senate.

The former Anambra State governor said the discussions focused on Nigeria’s development, national security, economic prosperity, citizens’ welfare and the future of the country’s democracy.

Among the American personalities he met were Congressmen Marlin Stutzman and Todd Tiahrt, Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne, Suzanne Bock Grisham and retired US Army Colonel Albert V. Short.

A major highlight of the visit was his address on Capitol Hill, where he emphasised the importance of international cooperation in advancing Nigeria’s national unity, security and economic development.

Obi also stressed the need to protect Nigeria’s democracy and strengthen democratic institutions to guarantee free, fair, transparent and credible elections ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He maintained that Nigerians must determine the country’s future, insisting that every vote must count and the rights of citizens must be protected.

The NDC presidential candidate also held an interview with American television commentator Glenn Beck, during which they discussed Nigeria’s leadership challenges, accountability, resource management and development prospects.

Obi reaffirmed his commitment to working with Nigerians at home and in the diaspora, as well as international partners, towards building a peaceful, secure and prosperous country.

text:
A retired Air Force pilot and 16-year Delta veteran is sounding the alarm: America's air traffic control system is "broken" and "archaic," and Friday's historic FAA ground stop will not be the last.

Retired Lt. Col. Buzz Patterson, who carried the nuclear football for former President Bill Clinton, tells Fox News Digital that both parties have "kicked the can" for decades on a desperately needed overhaul. The result? Facilities still running on floppy disks, controllers using paper scripts to taxi airplanes, and 1970s-era technology managing skies packed with modern traffic.

"We're putting Americans in danger when they get into an airplane, and we're putting the air crews in danger when they get into an airplane, if we continue to fly under archaic system," Patterson says. He warns the next meltdown could hit on Thanksgiving Eve or Christmas Eve, and says he doesn't feel safe putting his own family on an airplane until Washington commits to fixing it.
